event_title: Appling Solar Farm Construction Begins
event_description: Construction commenced on the 25-megawatt Appling Solar Farm in Appling County, Georgia. The project was developed by Silicon Ranch with IEA as the construction contractor. Approximately 150 local workers were recruited to construct the facility over 8 months. The solar farm is part of a portfolio providing 100% renewable energy to Meta's Newton Data Center.

event_title: Appling Solar Farm Begins Generating Power for Meta Data Center
event_description: The 25-megawatt Appling Solar Farm in Appling County began generating power, completing construction on schedule before the end of 2020. The facility is part of a portfolio of Silicon Ranch projects providing 100% renewable energy to Walton EMC for Facebook/Meta's data center in Newton County. The solar farm also features Silicon Ranch's Regenerative Energy land management program.

event_title: Amazon announces $11B Georgia investment
event_description: Largest corporate announcement in Georgia history. Split between Butts and Douglas counties. 550+ high-skilled jobs expected.

event_title: Bartow Planning Commission recommends denial of Springbank
event_description: $4.5B Atlas Development project near Barnsley Resort denied. ~1,700 petition signatures; concerns about tourism jobs. 'Good idea, wrong location.'

event_title: $19B Project Bunkhouse approved with conditions
event_description: Planning Commission recommended approval of 8.6M sf, 12-building campus on 876 acres. Development Authority declined to offer incentives.

event_title: County Officials Discuss Data Center Zoning Preparedness
event_description: Macon-Bibb County Planning and Zoning Executive Director Jeff Ruggieri confirmed that while no formal data center applications have been received, the county's existing zoning code can handle such proposals. Data centers would be classified as heavy industrial use requiring conditional use permits. Mayor Lester Miller stated he would only support data centers in commercial areas away from residential neighborhoods, citing concerns about other counties' experiences with data center impacts.

event_title: EdgePresence Deploys First Multi-Tenant Data Center in Statesboro
event_description: EdgePresence announced the deployment of a new edge data center in Statesboro, marking the first multi-tenant data center available in the city. The 360 sq ft facility at 695 Brannen Street features SOC II certification and turnkey infrastructure, providing edge computing and traditional colocation services. The facility operates at 0.1 MW capacity and serves businesses in southern Georgia and northern Florida.

event_title: Bulloch Solutions Partners with EdgePresence for Edge Infrastructure
event_description: Bulloch Solutions, a local technology provider in Statesboro, announced a partnership with EdgePresence to offer new edge data center solutions to customers in the Bulloch County region. The partnership enables Bulloch Solutions to leverage EdgePresence's micro data center infrastructure at 695 Brannen Street to provide hosted managed services, e-commerce, IoT, and cloud solutions to local businesses.

event_title: Ubiquity Acquires EdgePresence Including Statesboro Facility
event_description: Digital infrastructure firm Ubiquity acquired EdgePresence, including the Statesboro edge data center facility. The acquisition brought EdgePresence's 11 deployed facilities under Ubiquity's management. The Statesboro facility continues to operate as part of Ubiquity's Edge business unit, which focuses on localized assets adjacent to end users.

event_title: Villa Rica Approves Technology Park Overlay District for Data Centers
event_description: The Villa Rica City Council voted 4-1 to approve a technology park overlay district that would allow data centers within city limits. Councilmember Shirley Marchman voted in opposition. The overlay district was described as an addition to zoning code that defines what can be built, density requirements, setback distances, and compliance requirements. Several members of the public spoke in opposition during the meeting.

event_title: Community Opposition at Villa Rica Council Meeting on Data Center Rezoning
event_description: Villa Rica citizens expressed significant opposition at the city council meeting regarding rezoning that would allow data centers. The introduction of the rezoning item was followed by what was described as an outburst from the audience. Joe Fowler spoke for applicant Mike Embry, explaining that the PUD overlay would define building parameters and require staff review of every site plan with public hearings.

event_title: Atlas Development Files DRI for 428-Acre Avemore Data Center Campus
event_description: Atlas Development submitted a Development of Regional Impact (DRI) application to the Georgia Department of Community Affairs for Avemore, a proposed 428-acre technology and data park in Villa Rica. The project envisions up to seven single-story data center buildings, each approximately 350,000 square feet, totaling 2.45 million square feet. The estimated investment ranges between $5 billion and $7 billion with first phase anticipated to commence in 2028.

event_title: Planning and Zoning Commission Hearing on Atlas Development Data Center Proposal
event_description: The Villa Rica Planning and Zoning Commission held a public hearing on Atlas Development's proposed data center project. The commission clarified that Atlas Development is distinct from Embry Development. Residents raised concerns about water consumption, traffic congestion, and the transformation of residential areas into industrial zones. The project would replace a previously approved 2000-home residential development.

event_title: Villa Rica Approves Annexation and Rezoning for Avemore Data Center
event_description: The Villa Rica City Council voted to approve the annexation and rezoning of property for the Avemore data center project despite several members of the public speaking in opposition. Residents expressed concerns about water usage estimated at 1.1 million gallons per day, infrastructure impacts, and the location in a residential area. Carroll County School Superintendent spoke in favor of the project over residential development.

event_title: 500-Signature Petition Filed Against Villa Rica Data Center
event_description: Local residents including Paul Cutler and Dan Christner collected approximately 500 signatures on door-to-door petitions opposing the proposed data center development near South Van Wert Road and Highway 61. Residents cited concerns about the data center being placed in a longstanding residential area with approximately 12 residential communities nearby.

event_title: Residents File Court Petition Against Villa Rica Data Center Approval
event_description: More than 30 Carroll County residents filed a petition in Carroll County Superior Court challenging the City of Villa Rica's annexation and rezoning of over 200 acres of land for the Avemore data center project. The petitioners, who are adjacent and adjoining landowners, allege procedural failures and omissions by Embry Development and the City of Villa Rica in the annexation and rezoning process.

event_title: Athens-Clarke passes emergency data center moratorium
event_description: Commission unanimously approved temporary emergency moratorium until March 6, 2026 following denial of 2M sf proposal. 25-year-old zoning code lacks data center definition.

event_title: Odom Solar Farm Construction Begins to Power Facebook Data Center
event_description: Silicon Ranch Corporation and PCL Construction announced commencement of construction on the 20-megawatt Odom Solar Farm located near Moultrie in Colquitt County. The solar farm is part of a portfolio providing power to Walton EMC as part of the utility's agreement to supply 100 percent renewable energy for Facebook's data center in Newton County. Barbara Grogan, President of the Moultrie Colquitt County Development Authority, welcomed both Silicon Ranch and PCL Construction to the community.

event_title: White Oak Technology Park DRI Filed with State
event_description: Trammell Crow Co., a subsidiary of commercial real estate giant CBRE, filed a Development of Regional Impact (DRI) application with the Georgia Department of Community Affairs for the White Oak Technology Park. The proposal includes 29 data center buildings totaling 8 million square feet on 1,945 acres near Morris Callaway Road and Innovation Parkway. The estimated build-out value is $11.6 billion with projected annual tax revenue exceeding $118 million.

event_title: Planning Commission Approves S-1 Rezoning for Data Center Site
event_description: The Columbia County Planning Commission unanimously approved a request from the Economic Development Authority of Columbia County to rezone 1,945 acres behind White Oak Business Park from residential-agricultural to S-1 (Special Use) zoning. This rezoning enables data center, research and development, and cybersecurity uses on the property.

event_title: Development Authority Launches Public Information Website for Data Center Project
event_description: The Economic Development Authority of Columbia County launched a new website to provide public information about the White Oak Technology Park project. Executive Director Cheney Eldridge stated the site aims to address resident concerns about water usage, power infrastructure, and environmental impacts, emphasizing transparency without advocating for any particular position.

event_title: Appling Residents Voice Opposition to Data Center Plans
event_description: Residents near the proposed White Oak Technology Park site expressed concerns about the project, claiming they were not adequately informed about the plans. Resident Alan Wyatt stated he discovered the project encompasses 3 square miles of industrial development. Concerns included noise, water usage, and impacts on rural character. Some residents met with commissioners who indicated the development could reduce property taxes.

event_title: PSC Commissioner Discusses Data Center at Campaign Stop
event_description: Georgia Public Service Commissioner Tim Echols made a campaign stop in Columbia County where the proposed data center became the main topic of discussion. Echols expressed support for the project's potential revenue benefits while acknowledging resident concerns. Some attendees remained on the fence, requesting more information about impacts from communities with existing data centers.

event_title: Planning Commission Recommends Data Center Zoning District to Board
event_description: The Columbia County Planning Commission voted to recommend approval of a text amendment creating a new DC (Data Center) zoning district. The proposed ordinance includes a 70-decibel noise limit, 500-foot buffers from residential properties, and restrictions on generator testing. Approximately 15 residents spoke during public comment, most opposing the new district. The ordinance was forwarded to the Board of Commissioners.

event_title: Board of Commissioners Holds First Reading of DC Zoning Ordinance
event_description: Columbia County commissioners conducted the first reading of the proposed data center zoning ordinance following months of public debate. The proposed guidelines establish 75-foot maximum building height, 500-foot natural buffers from residential properties, and 70-decibel noise limits. Despite resident concerns about noise and water usage, commissioners unanimously approved moving the proposal to final reading on December 2.

event_title: Georgia Power Approves Power Consumption Model for White Oak Project
event_description: Chairman Douglas Duncan announced that Georgia Power has approved the proposed power consumption model for the White Oak Technology Park data center project. This approval brings the county closer to securing an end user for the project. Duncan stated that all infrastructure and utility costs will be borne by the end user with no financial burden on residents. Land acquisition is anticipated to complete before December 19.

event_title: Blockstream Bitcoin Mining Facility Opens in Adel
event_description: Blockstream revealed its Bitcoin mining data center facility in Adel, Georgia with 270 MW capacity. The facility uses a colocation model with customers including Fidelity Center for Applied Technology and LinkedIn co-founder Reid Hoffman. Power is supplied by the City of Adel municipal utility.

event_title: City of Adel Signs MOU with Blockstream on Noise Limits
event_description: The City of Adel signed a Memorandum of Understanding with Blockstream establishing that the facility must maintain noise levels at or below 60 decibels when measured 500 feet from the mining operation.

event_title: Blockstream Announces Expansion and 84-Acre Land Purchase
event_description: Blockstream announced expansion of its Bitcoin mining data center in Cook County. The company purchased 84 acres at Exit 45 using Federal Opportunity Zone and New Market Tax Credits. Plans include building a substation to generate additional power for expanded operations.

event_title: City of Adel Receives Visionary City Award for Blockstream Power Deal
event_description: The City of Adel partnered with six other MEAG communities to sell their excess power to Blockstream, enabling the Bitcoin mining operation. The Georgia Municipal Association recognized Adel with the Visionary City Award for this arrangement.

event_title: BlockFi Announces Bitcoin Mining Partnership with Blockstream Adel Facility
event_description: Bitcoin lending platform BlockFi announced plans to host bitcoin mining operations with Blockstream Mining at the Adel, Georgia facility. The facility offers 300 MW of power capacity with cooling and air filtration technology for mining operations.

event_title: Wall Street Journal Highlights Resident Noise Complaints Against Blockstream
event_description: The Wall Street Journal published an article titled 'Bitcoin Mining Noise Drives Neighbors Nuts—a Giant Dentist Drill That Won't Stop' featuring complaints from Adel residents including Annette and Ron Tiveron. Blockstream's mining head Chris Cook described the facility as 'barely audible' and 'quieter than crickets,' disputed by residents.

event_title: WFXL Reports on Adel Residents Pleading for Help with Bitcoin Noise
event_description: Local television station WFXL reported on Adel residents pleading for help after the loud Bitcoin mining operation moved into their community. Residents described health impacts including hearing damage from the constant noise.

event_title: Blockstream Shuts Down Bitcoin Mining Units Due to High Energy Costs
event_description: During the Adel City Council meeting, City Manager John Flythe announced that Blockstream shut down its mining units due to projected energy costs exceeding 14 cents per kilowatt. The shutdown was expected to last at least 8 months, resulting in loss of $240,000-$320,000 in school system sales tax revenue.

event_title: Project Peach approved 3-2 despite opposition
event_description: $1B, 2.1M sf data center approved with 27 conditions. Palmetto Mayor Teresa Thomas-Smith opposed the project.

event_title: Coweta County extends moratorium to December 17
event_description: Board signed resolution extending 180-day moratorium to earliest of December 17, 2025 or adoption of land use amendments. Project Sail remains pending.

event_title: Red Wolf DCD Proposes Project Splice Data Center Campus
event_description: Red Wolf DCD Properties LLC unveiled plans for Project Splice, a $6 billion technology campus featuring seven 300,000 sq ft buildings totaling 2.1 million sq ft. The project would be built in three phases through 2033 near I-75 Exit 102 in Crisp County.

event_title: Public Hearing on Red Wolf Project Splice Rezoning Request
event_description: Crisp County Board of Commissioners held a public hearing on Red Wolf Properties' request to rezone 583.62 acres from rural residential to general commercial. Residents voiced opposition citing concerns about noise, traffic, electricity rates, and impacts during construction. Project consultant Andy Camp explained the closed-loop cooling system and job creation of 180-200 positions.

event_title: Crisp County Unanimously Approves Project Splice Data Center Rezoning
event_description: Crisp County Board of Commissioners unanimously approved Red Wolf Properties' rezoning request for the Project Splice data center campus. The approval included conditions on noise limits, lighting, construction hours, fire response plans, and requirements that agricultural wells not be used for commercial operations.

event_title: Georgia DCA approves new data center DRI thresholds
event_description: Board unanimously approved 'technological facilities' category: 500,000 sf outside Atlanta, 300,000 sf in metro areas triggers Development of Regional Impact review.

event_title: Hotel Gordon Blockchain Data Center Approved by Downtown Development Authority
event_description: The Albany Downtown Development Authority unanimously approved a redevelopment plan for 207 Pine Avenue including an 88-room boutique hotel, rooftop restaurant, and blockchain technology data center. Developer J Car Development LLC proposed a $13.6 million investment creating 43 jobs. The City Commission approved a $3 million loan the following day. The project later failed during COVID-19 pandemic due to developer illness and financing challenges.

event_title: Douglas County passes 90-day moratorium
event_description: 4-1 vote despite county being 'birthplace of Georgia data centers.' Commissioner Raxton: opportunity to align with comprehensive plan.

event_title: QTS Data Centers Initiates Project Blue Hole Discussions with Blakely
event_description: McKnight Engler contacted the City of Blakely to discuss a potential data center project. After internal research confirmed the McKnight-Blakely property would be suitable, discussions began with local economic development officials about bringing a QTS data center to the community.

event_title: Rickey Stokes News Reports QTS Exploring Data Center in Blakely
event_description: Regional news outlet Rickey Stokes News reported that QTS Data Centers is exploring opportunities to establish new data center campuses in Blakely, Georgia, emphasizing QTS's commitment to community partnership and economic growth.

event_title: Early County News Publishes Detailed Q&A on QTS Project Blue Hole
event_description: The Early County News published a comprehensive Q&A with John Engler of McKnight-Blakely LLC and Susanne Reynolds of Blakely-Early County Economic Development about the proposed QTS data center. The article addressed community concerns about water, power, noise, jobs, and economic impacts. Local leadership confirmed they had toured QTS Atlanta facilities.

event_title: Fannin County Enacts Ban on Crypto Mining Operations
event_description: The Fannin County Commission enacted a ban on cryptocurrency mining operations, making it one of the only Georgia counties to outright prohibit such facilities. The ban came amid growing concerns across rural Georgia about the energy consumption and noise impacts of crypto mining server farms.

event_title: Data Center Developer Requests Conditional Use Permit Near GA-400
event_description: Viral Chhadua, a Gainesville native and data center developer with HadjPadj Technologies, requested a conditional use permit for a data center to be built near GA-400 in Forsyth County. The request came as data center interest in the county was growing.

event_title: Forsyth County Commission Considers Data Center Zoning Rules
event_description: At its November 26, 2024 work session, the Forsyth County Commission considered changes to the Unified Development Code that would require new data centers to observe rules governing noise, distance to homes, size, and utility usage. The proposed rules include 60-foot setbacks from homes, 20-foot height limits, and noise limits of 60 decibels (55 dB from 5am-7pm).

event_title: Forsyth County Adopts Restrictive Data Center Ordinance
event_description: Forsyth County adopted a data center ordinance that prohibits cooling systems from using the county water system. According to Chattahoochee Riverkeeper Water Policy Director Chris Manganiello, the Forsyth ordinance puts significant guardrails that may effectively eliminate any data center or crypto operation from setting up shop in the community.

event_title: Atlanta bans data centers near BeltLine
event_description: City Council voted unanimously to prohibit data centers within 22-mile BeltLine overlay and half-mile of MARTA rail stations.

event_title: Atlanta requires special-use permits for data centers
event_description: Bans data centers in Little Five Points, East Atlanta Village, Inman Park, Virginia-Highlands, Cascade Heights. 150K sf/floor limits elsewhere.

event_title: Gilmer County Defeats Proposed Crypto Server Farm Rezoning
event_description: Residents of Gilmer County beat back a proposed rezoning that would have allowed a cryptocurrency server farm in the rural community. Gilmer County Citizens Against Crypto Mining, co-founded by resident Cyndie Roberson, mobilized hundreds of residents to a planning commission meeting to oppose the project.

event_title: Gilmer County Becomes Only Georgia County with Crypto Mining Ban
event_description: Gilmer County adopted an ordinance banning cryptocurrency mining, making it the only Georgia county with such a prohibition. The ban followed successful community organizing efforts led by Cyndie Roberson and other local activists. The city of Ellijay also has restrictions on crypto operations.

event_title: City of Ellijay Adopts Crypto Mining Restrictions
event_description: The City of Ellijay, located within Gilmer County, adopted restrictions on crypto mining operations, complementing the county-wide ban on such facilities.

event_title: Glynn County Commission Considers Data Center Ordinance
event_description: The Glynn County Board of Commissioners held a special called meeting to consider a proposed data center ordinance. The ordinance would define data centers as a permitted use in limited, basic, and general industrial zones. Provisions include 75-foot building height limits, buffer requirements, air conditioning and HVAC system standards, facade requirements, and security fencing specifications. This is a proactive measure as no data center proposals are currently pending in the county.

event_title: Big Red Apple Innovation Corridor Data Center Proposal Filed
event_description: The Cook and Company of Gainesville submitted a Development of Regional Impact form for the Big Red Apple Innovation Corridor, a 284-acre mixed-use development that includes a data center component. The property is located at 1900 Level Grove Road near Cornelia off GA-365. The $300 million project would include residential, commercial, retail, and industrial components with completion targeted for 2026-2035. The City of Cornelia would supply an estimated 1.5 million gallons of water per day.

event_title: $1.2B Project Turbo withdrawn from Hall County
event_description: Developer withdrew special use permit application citing 'insufficient fact-finding' at commission level. Gainesville confirmed inadequate water capacity for project.

event_title: Perry Proposes Text Amendment to Restrict Data Centers to M-2 Zoning
event_description: The Perry City Council held a first reading on a text amendment to the land management ordinance that would add data centers as a use permitted only by special exception in the M-2 Industrial Zoning district. Community Development Director Bryan Wood stated the city is being proactive in restricting data centers. Mayor Randall Walker noted the city lacks the water and electricity infrastructure to support data centers. No vote was taken as this was the first reading.

event_title: Jones County adopts strict data center ordinance
event_description: Requirements include closed-loop cooling, crypto mining ban, 45/35 dB noise limits, 100-ft buffers, HVAC concealment. Later rescinded November 2025 due to legal issues.

event_title: Jones County rescinds data center ordinance due to legal issues
event_description: County rescinded strict zoning ordinances adopted in September due to legal concerns about procedural requirements.

event_title: Monroe County unanimously rejects Bolingbroke Tech Center
event_description: 900+ red-shirted residents packed meeting. $5.8B, 900-acre project denied unanimously. Landowners filed lawsuit alleging violation of zoning procedures.

event_title: Google purchases 948 acres in Monroe County
event_description: Google closed on $42.6M purchase of land at Rumble Road adjacent to approved Rumble Technology Campus for future data center development.

event_title: Monroe County passes data center moratorium
event_description: 4-1 vote establishing moratorium until March 2026 commission meeting. Does not apply to City of Forsyth projects. 'Groton solution' under consideration.

event_title: Synovus $22M Technology Center Announced for Columbus
event_description: Synovus Financial Corp. announced plans to build a $22 million data center in Columbus on Moon Road. The 50,000 square foot facility is expandable to 100,000 square feet on a 10.5-acre site. Construction was expected to complete within approximately one year of the announcement.

event_title: Cave Spring City Council Considers 120-Day Data Center Moratorium
event_description: The Cave Spring City Council discussed a possible 120-day moratorium on data centers to allow for a feasibility study. City Manager Josh Shoaf stated the moratorium would only apply within city limits and is intended to study how to prevent data center development in the southern part of the county. No formal vote was taken at this meeting.

event_title: QTS Fayetteville construction progresses
event_description: 615-acre, 7M sf, 250+ MW campus under construction. Microsoft Fairwater AI superfactory to be first tenant.

event_title: T5 Data Centers Announces T5@Augusta Campus Near Fort Gordon
event_description: T5 Data Centers announced plans for a 140-acre government and enterprise cloud data center campus adjacent to Fort Gordon (now Fort Eisenhower). The proposed development would offer 200MW of capacity. Augusta Economic Development Authority Chairman Steven Kendrick stated the development would help spur more tech-centric economic development for the community.

event_title: Richmond County Planning Commission Approves Initial T5 Rezoning
event_description: The Richmond County Planning Commission voted to approve rezoning a more than 200-acre tract at 2111 Powell Road from Agricultural and Manufactured Home Residential to General Business for T5 Data Centers. The proposed development included a two-story, 350,000-square-foot data warehouse building. The project required a Developments of Regional Impact (DRI) study coordinated with the CSRA Regional Commission.

event_title: Eagle South LLC Files Revised DRI for Project Eisenhower
event_description: Eagle South LLC filed a revised Development of Regional Impact (DRI) application with the Georgia Department of Community Affairs for Project Eisenhower, an expanded version of the former T5@Augusta campus. The project would consist of six two-story buildings totaling 2.15 million square feet on Gordon Highway. T5 Data Centers confirmed it is no longer involved in developing the site. First phase construction targeted for Q2 2026.

event_title: Augusta Planning Commission Unanimously Approves Project Eisenhower Rezoning
event_description: The Augusta Planning Commission unanimously voted to recommend rezoning 165.21 acres at 2883 Gordon Highway from Agricultural and General Business to only General Business for Project Eisenhower data center. Developer Eagle South LLC and property owner Vitrified Brick & Clay Co. represented by attorney Darren Meadows. Project represents $2 billion investment with 620 construction jobs and 160-220 permanent positions.

event_title: Spalding County Adopts Data Center Zoning Text Amendments
event_description: The Spalding County Board of Commissioners approved second readings of text amendments introducing the term 'data center' to county code, defining data centers, and making them a permitted use in PDD (Planned Development District - Industrial Park) zoning. The amendments were designed to facilitate intelligent location of data centers with proper buffering and architectural standards while protecting residential areas.

event_title: Project Spalding DRI Application Filed with Georgia DCA
event_description: Montana Property Group LLC filed a Development of Regional Impact (DRI) application with the Georgia Department of Community Affairs for Project Spalding, a 2.56 million square foot data center campus on approximately 133 acres on High Falls Road. The DRI listed estimated value at buildout of $1.875 billion and projected annual local tax revenues of $26.859 million.

event_title: Spalding County Resident Raises Alarm About Proposed Data Center
event_description: Greg Berns, a Spalding County resident, spoke during the Citizen Comment portion of the BOC meeting expressing concern about the 2.5 million square foot data center proposal. He questioned why there had been no public discourse about the project and referenced the DRI application filed by Montana Property Group.

event_title: Spalding County Planning Commission Reviews Data Center Rezoning
event_description: The Spalding County Planning Commission held a public hearing on the proposal by 585 Spalding Investments LLC to rezone 127.459 acres from agricultural residential and single-family residential to C1C manufacturing for a data center. The commission recommended approval with conditions.

event_title: Spalding County BOC Approves First Data Center 4-1
event_description: The Spalding County Board of Commissioners approved rezonings 4-1 and special exceptions unanimously for the first data center in the county. The project by Montana Property Group LLC covers 132.9 acres on High Falls Road and Alicia Drive. District 1 Commissioner Gwen Flowers-Taylor cast the dissenting votes on rezonings. The project falls within the county's Employment Character Area and will feature closed-loop water systems.

event_title: Montana Property Group Presents Data Center Plans to BOC
event_description: Montana Property Group representatives presented detailed plans for the 140-acre data center site along High Falls Road adjacent to the future airport site. The hearing addressed access points, security measures, and the single entrance requirement. Commissioners discussed emergency response access and buffer requirements.

event_title: Second Data Center Rezoning Tabled by BOC
event_description: The Spalding County BOC tabled the rezoning and special exception for the second data center project by Spalding Investments LLC to work out concerns with zoning, timeframe, and conditions. The original proposal for eight buildings was redesigned to six buildings to address airport flight path height restrictions.

event_title: Second Data Center Approved Unanimously with 23 Conditions
event_description: The Spalding County BOC unanimously approved the second data center on 127.45 acres bordered by High Falls Road, South McDonough Road, and Highway 16. Spalding Investments LLC redesigned from 8 to 6 buildings (1.42 million sq ft total) with 23 conditions including: FAA approval for height restrictions, acoustics/noise studies, acoustic walls around generators, closed-loop water systems, 4-foot berm with 6-foot evergreen trees for buffering, and decommissioning requirements.

event_title: Community Opposition Presented at Second Data Center Hearing
event_description: Despite approval, residents presented opposition including emotional pleas, a video showing problems caused by data centers elsewhere in Georgia, an audio recording of data center noise levels, and a petition against the project with 289 signatures. The BOC approved the project despite this opposition.

event_title: Switch files DRI for $772M second Georgia campus
event_description: KEEP 2.0 Atlanta North Campus on 126 acres. 1,200 MW commitment via Georgia EMC. Phase 1 expected Q2 2026.

event_title: T5 acquires 91-acre site in South Fulton
event_description: 1.32M sf, 200 MW campus planned. Substation operational 2026, Phase 1 delivery 2027.

event_title: Thor Equities Acquires 270-Acre Site for Project Pegasus
event_description: Thor Equities Group acquired a 270-acre parcel at 411 Pegasus Parkway, the former Jindal Films site, for data center development. The site includes a 506,220 sq ft facility with a dedicated substation capable of 100 MVA transformation and 50 MW of in-place power, plus existing transformers, water, sewer, and natural gas infrastructure.

event_title: Project West $9.7 Billion Data Center Campus DRI Filed
event_description: Developer Joshua Harrelson filed a Development of Regional Impact for Project West, a six-building data center campus across 513 acres in unincorporated Troup County. The project would have capacity for 600 MW and generate an estimated $60 million in annual tax revenue. The DRI requested annexation into the City of LaGrange.

event_title: LaGrange City Council Fails to Approve Project West Annexation
event_description: LaGrange City Council did not move forward with annexing and rezoning 513 acres for Project West. Debate centered on the massive electrical power requirements (600 MW, roughly six times the city's current usage) and concerns that data centers would drive up electricity costs for residents. No motion was made to proceed with county notification.

event_title: Environmental Groups Host Data Center Town Hall at LaGrange Library
event_description: Representatives from Science for Georgia, Chattahoochee Riverkeeper, and Sierra Club held a standing-room-only town hall at LaGrange Memorial Library to discuss data center impacts. Dr. Amy Sharma noted Project Pegasus received a 50% tax abatement for 20 years and would create fewer than 50 jobs. Speakers encouraged residents to push for moratoriums and strong ordinances.

event_title: Troup County Approves 90-Day Data Center Moratorium
event_description: The Troup County Board of Commissioners unanimously approved a 90-day moratorium on data center applications in unincorporated areas. During the pause, staff will study data center impacts and draft amendments to the Unified Development Ordinance. The moratorium does not affect LaGrange, Hogansville, or West Point jurisdictions.

event_title: Chattahoochee Riverkeeper Requests LaGrange Moratorium
event_description: Chattahoochee Riverkeeper sent a letter to Mayor Jim Arrington and LaGrange City Council requesting a 90-day moratorium on data center development. The letter cited Douglas County's approach as a model and noted that proposed data centers in LaGrange and Troup County represent unprecedented impact on water and energy resources.

event_title: LaGrange City Council Passes 180-Day Moratorium on Data Centers
event_description: LaGrange City Council voted to issue a 180-day moratorium on new data center applications, proposed by Mayor Jim Arrington. The moratorium allows staff to develop regulations for the Unified Development Ordinance. Project Pegasus at 411 Pegasus Parkway is unaffected as it has vested rights from prior approvals and bond validation.

event_title: LaGrange approves 180-day data center moratorium
event_description: Project Pegasus unaffected (permits already approved). 150 parcels currently allow data centers with no specific UDO regulations.

event_title: Hogansville Announces Developer Interest in Data Center on Hightower Road
event_description: The City of Hogansville announced via Facebook that a developer has expressed interest in constructing a data center on city-owned property on Hightower Road. Open records requests revealed Fertile Ground Investments LLC had signed an intergovernmental agreement and real estate purchase option in 2024 for 437 acres at $12,000 per acre, contingent on rezoning to industrial. MEAG conducted a power study for 600 MW.

event_title: Hogansville Residents Protest Data Center at Council Meeting
event_description: A standing-room-only crowd attended Hogansville City Council meeting to voice concerns about the proposed data center. Mayor Jake Ayers read a prepared statement emphasizing no decisions have been made. Gage Bailey of the Troup County Anti-Data Center Coalition attended with members holding protest signs. Mayor announced a town hall would be scheduled before any decisions.

event_title: Anti-Data Center Coalition Addresses Hogansville Council
event_description: Gage Bailey addressed Hogansville City Council during public comments, warning that residents on Hightower Road could lose homes to infrastructure development for transmission lines and substations. Bailey urged transparency and questioned what legacy city leaders wanted for Hogansville. Council set up feedback email and announced December 2 town hall.

event_title: Hogansville Holds Town Hall on Proposed Data Center
event_description: Hogansville held a town hall meeting at 7 p.m. following the council meeting to hear citizen concerns about the proposed 437-acre data center on Hightower Road. Residents raised concerns about property devaluation, utility bill increases, lack of jobs (30-35 projected), and impacts on neighboring properties including a 30-acre zoo.

event_title: Troup County Extends Data Center Moratorium 90 Days
event_description: The Troup County Board of Commissioners unanimously extended the data center moratorium for an additional 90 days to align with LaGrange's moratorium expiration in March 2026. County Attorney Mark Degennaro cited the need for more time to finalize the draft ordinance and coordinate with LaGrange, Hogansville, and West Point.

event_title: Troup County Presents Draft Data Center Ordinance
event_description: County Attorney Mark Degennaro presented a very rough, first-cut draft of a data center ordinance during the work session. The draft addresses zoning districts, parcel sizes, and other regulations. Staff noted the need to coordinate with LaGrange and distinguish between traditional data centers and crypto mining operations.

event_title: Twiggs County approves 900 MW Pine Ridge Tech Park
event_description: Commission unanimously approved rezoning for 291-acre hyperscale facility with power demand equal to Macon plus Augusta. Decision 'met with boos and applause.'

event_title: Sailfish Investors annexation approved
event_description: Walton County commissioners approved annexation for $1.7B, 1.78M sf data center to be developed by Sailfish Investors.

event_title: Social Circle enacts 90-day data center moratorium
event_description: City unanimously passed moratorium to 'work through data center requests already in hand.' City Manager: 'It's coming too fast, too soon.'

event_title: Atlas Development approved despite Planning denial
event_description: Social Circle City Council overrode Planning Commission's unanimous denial with 2-1 vote for 1.5M sf, 288 MW data center. Nearly 100 people attended.

event_title: Dermody PL data center approved in Social Circle
event_description: City Council approved four 250,000 sf buildings plus 100,000 sf substation on 96 acres. First building 2-3 years; full build-out 5 years.

event_title: Mawson Infrastructure Group Opens Bitcoin Mining Facility in Sandersville
event_description: Mawson Infrastructure Group, an Australian-based digital infrastructure provider, opened its first bitcoin mining facility in Washington County. The company signed a lease for approximately one acre in the Fall Line Industrial Park in Sandersville, working with MEAG and Electrical Cities of Georgia for power supply.

event_title: Ribbon Cutting Celebrates Mawson Expansion in Washington County
event_description: A ribbon cutting ceremony was held for the expanded Mawson bitcoin mining facility in Washington County. The company made a $76 million investment and became Sandersville's second-largest electric utility customer. City Administrator Judy McCorkle praised the company's community support and expansion plans.

event_title: Mawson Announces Expansion to 230 MW in Sandersville
event_description: Mawson Infrastructure Group announced approval to expand its Sandersville facility from 80 MW to 230 MW. Following successful electrical load and infrastructure studies by MEAG, ECG, and local authorities, the site was approved for major expansion. The facility has a 26-year lease with option to purchase the 16-acre property. Expansion expected online by Q3 2023.

event_title: CleanSpark Acquires Sandersville Bitcoin Mining Facility
event_description: CleanSpark acquired the Mawson Sandersville facility, making it their largest site in the portfolio at the time. The turnkey operation was purchased from Mawson Infrastructure Group with room to almost triple its capacity. The facility became part of CleanSpark's expanding Georgia footprint.

event_title: CleanSpark Acquires Five Additional Cryptomine Sites in Georgia
event_description: CleanSpark announced acquisition of five additional bitcoin mining sites in Georgia ranging from 8MW to 15MW, totaling 60MW. After the Sandersville location is fully energized and acquired sites go live, CleanSpark will operate more than 400MW of infrastructure in Georgia. This expansion reinforces Washington County's role as a hub for CleanSpark operations.

event_title: Core Scientific Announces $42M Crypto Mining Facility in Dalton
event_description: Core Scientific announced plans to develop a $42 million cryptomining facility on the site of a vacant factory in Dalton, Georgia. The initial facility had operational capacity of 20-35 MW before planned expansion to 170 MW. This marked the beginning of significant data center development in Whitfield County.

event_title: Core Scientific Dalton Facility Becomes Large Dalton Utilities Customer
event_description: The Core Scientific facility in Dalton became a major electricity customer for Dalton Utilities. Prior to data center operations, Dalton Utilities had peak load demand of 275 MW. The facility sources power from Dalton Utilities, which uses predominantly nuclear and hydro energy sources.

event_title: Core Scientific Expands Dalton Facility to 170 MW
event_description: Core Scientific expanded its Whitfield County facility to full 170 MW capacity, with multiple buildings across the Dalton area. The company's Dalton footprint eventually grew to approximately 195 MW across multiple facilities (Dalton 1 at 50MW and Dalton 3 at 145MW).

event_title: Core Scientific Purchases 173 Acres on Old Tilton Road for Data Center
event_description: Core Scientific purchased 173.3 acres of land on Old Tilton Road in Dalton for $3.6 million. The property, located southeast of Dalton near the Murray County line, was acquired for development of a new AI-focused data center facility.

event_title: Planning Commission Hearing on Core Scientific Rezoning Draws Concerns
event_description: The Dalton-Varnell-Whitfield County Planning Commission held a meeting on the rezoning request for the Core Scientific AI data center site. Several residents expressed concern about the data center's potential impact on local electrical rates. The planning commission process revealed community concerns about utility impacts.

event_title: Whitfield County Approves Rezoning for AI Data Center 3-2 Despite Opposition
event_description: Whitfield County Board of Commissioners voted 3-2 to approve Core Scientific's request to rezone 173.3 acres from general agriculture and rural residential to heavy manufacturing. The decision was greeted with loud and sustained jeers from the crowd. Commissioners Staten and Jones voted for; Thomas and Robbins voted against; Chairman Jensen cast the tie-breaking vote for approval. A condition requires access to Enterprise Drive to reduce traffic impact.

event_title: Core Scientific Plans New AI Data Centers in Dalton Announced
event_description: Data Center Dynamics reported on Core Scientific's plans for new AI data centers in Dalton. The company plans a two-pronged approach: converting one existing crypto mining facility to AI-focused operations, and tearing down another to build new purpose-built AI infrastructure. The new data center represents approximately $200 million investment.

event_title: County Officials Tout Data Center as Revenue Generator at Chamber Event
event_description: Whitfield County Commissioner Barry Robbins spoke at Greater Dalton Chamber of Commerce State of the Community breakfast, calling the AI data center a 'win' for the county. He emphasized economic diversification and school funding benefits from new tax revenue. County Administrator Robert Sivick said the data center is expected to buy $5 million monthly in electricity. Dalton Utilities CEO John Thomas stated data center costs would not be allocated to other customers.

event_title: Dalton Utilities Reports Peak Load Nearly Doubled Due to Data Centers
event_description: Dalton Utilities Chief Operating Officer Mark Buckner revealed at a League of Women Voters meeting that the utility's peak load has nearly doubled since data centers arrived, from about 250 MW to 476 MW. The utility now bills the largest data center weekly, with power bills averaging $1-1.5 million each week.

event_title: Dalton-Whitfield JDA Approves Tax Abatements for Core Scientific AI Data Center
event_description: The Dalton-Whitfield Joint Development Authority unanimously voted to formalize tax abatements for the Core Scientific AI data center through bonds-for-title agreements. The roughly $200 million investment will benefit from tax abatements on equipment, buildings, and land during the project term. JDA Executive Director Carl Campbell explained this is standard practice in Georgia where direct tax breaks are prohibited.

event_title: Utility Provider Inquiry Triggers Urgent Code Review in Lumpkin County
event_description: A utility provider contacted Lumpkin County about a subdivision that would require a massive amount of electricity, which Commission Chairman Chris Dockery said prompted the county to revisit its code book with "a sense of urgency." This inquiry was the catalyst for the county to proactively develop data center regulations before any formal proposals were made.

event_title: Lumpkin County Adopts Restrictive Compute Center Ordinance
event_description: Lumpkin County adopted a proactive "compute center" ordinance establishing strict regulations for data centers and cryptocurrency mining facilities before any projects were proposed. The ordinance uses an all-inclusive definition covering both data centers and crypto mines, and requires water discharge temperatures not exceed 41°F for cold-water fisheries or 37.4°F for warm-water fisheries. This ordinance was designed to protect the county's designated cold-water trout streams, which cover approximately half the county. The Chattahoochee Riverkeeper noted the ordinance puts "significant guardrails that may effectively eliminate any data center or crypto operation from setting up shop."

event_title: Chairman Dockery Explains Why Data Centers Aren't Good Fit for Lumpkin County
event_description: In an interview with Georgia Public Broadcasting, Lumpkin County Commission Chairman Chris Dockery explained the county's rationale for its restrictive ordinance. Dockery stated that data centers "aren't a good fit in Lumpkin County" because "they don't produce a lot of jobs and the topography of the land isn't conducive to big data centers." He also cited limited public water availability and the presence of designated cold-water trout streams in half the county as key factors in the decision to effectively prohibit large-scale data center development.

event_title: Bartow County Adopts Data Center Ordinance with Buffer and Noise Requirements
event_description: Bartow County adopted a data center-specific ordinance requiring 200-foot buffer zones and noise limits of 65dB daytime and 55dB nighttime. County administrator Peter Olsen stated the county remains pro-data center while implementing reasonable restrictions.

event_title: Adairsville Residents Launch Stop the Data Center Campaign Against Project Springbank
event_description: Residents near Barnsley Gardens Road in Adairsville organized opposition to Atlas Development's Project Springbank. Over 1,700 signatures collected on petition. Stop the Data Center signs posted throughout area. Concerns include noise, water runoff, and preservation of rural character.

event_title: Atlas Development Town Hall for Project Springbank
event_description: Atlas Development held town hall with Adairsville residents to discuss Project Springbank proposal. Attorney Brandon Bowen addressed concerns about noise and water runoff, stating data centers must follow all county ordinances.

event_title: Planning Commission Hearing on Project Springbank Rezoning
event_description: Bartow Planning and Zoning Commission heard rezoning request for Project Springbank at courthouse. Developers seek to rezone land from agricultural to industrial for 588-acre, $4.5B data center campus with six buildings and 2.274 million sq ft.

event_title: Project Bunkhouse $19B Data Center Campus Proposed for Stilesboro
event_description: Taurus DC SPE LLC and Digital Realty proposed Project Bunkhouse, an 876-acre, 8.6 million sq ft data center campus requiring 1,830MW of power. The $19B project would be one of the largest in Georgia if approved.

event_title: Switch North Campus $772M Expansion Announced Near LakePoint
event_description: Switch announced plans for $772 million North Campus expansion near LakePoint Sports complex in Bartow County, building on existing Cartersville operations.

event_title: Amazon AWS Announces $11B Investment in Butts and Douglas Counties
event_description: Amazon Web Services announced $11 billion investment to expand cloud computing and AI infrastructure in Georgia, with facilities in Butts and Douglas counties. Development Authority leased 543 acres to AWS. Chairman Russ Crumbley called it the most significant investment in Butts County history. Expected to create 550+ high-skilled jobs.

event_title: Clayton County Approves 120-Day Data Center Moratorium
event_description: Clayton County Board of Commissioners voted to impose 120-day moratorium on data centers through December 31, 2025 (Resolution 2025-193). Vice Chair Alaina Reaves sponsored the moratorium after residents raised concerns about electromagnetic fields and water supplies. Commission intends to study effects on health, safety, and welfare.

event_title: Ellenwood Data Center Approved with Closed-Loop Cooling
event_description: Data center approved in Ellenwood area using closed-loop water cooling process. According to Vice Chair Reaves, the closed-loop system recycles water so there isn't a draw on Clayton County's water supply.

event_title: Coweta County Approves 180-Day Moratorium on Data Centers
event_description: Coweta County Board of Commissioners voted for 180-day moratorium to draft zoning ordinance for data centers. Moratorium prompted by Project Sail proposal. Commissioners stated data centers are relatively new land use not explicitly addressed in most zoning codes.

event_title: Project Peach $1B Data Center Campus Approved 3-2
event_description: Coweta County commissioners approved rezoning for Project Peach, a $1 billion, 320-acre data center campus along Johnston Circle near Palmetto, in 3-2 vote. Project received opposition including from mayor of neighboring Palmetto in South Fulton County.

event_title: Citizens for Rural Coweta Files Petition with 1,750+ Signatures Against Project Sail
event_description: Citizens for Rural Coweta organized opposition to Project Sail and filed petition with over 1,750 signatures. Residents concerned about $17B, 831-acre campus proposed by Atlas Development along U.S. 27 between Welcome Sargent and Wager Mills roads.

event_title: Project Sail $17B Data Center Campus Proposed by Atlas Development
event_description: Atlas Development LLC proposed Project Sail, a $17 billion, 831-acre data center campus with 13 buildings and 4.9 million sq ft. Science for Georgia estimated project would use 750-950 MW of power (equivalent to 1.4 million households) and 3 billion gallons of water annually (population of Marietta).

event_title: DeKalb County Extends Data Center Moratorium to June 23, 2026
event_description: DeKalb County commissioners voted to extend data center moratorium to June 23, 2026. Commissioner Ted Terry proposed 12-month extension with $250K independent environmental study but motion failed 3-4. Public hearing scheduled for January 27, 2026.

event_title: DeKalb County Data Center Town Hall at Porter Sanford Arts Center
event_description: DeKalb County hosted town hall at Porter Sanford Performing Arts Center in Decatur to educate residents about data centers potentially being built near their neighborhoods. Event coincided with moratorium extension vote.

event_title: DeKalb County Extends Moratorium to December 16, 2025
event_description: DeKalb County commissioners voted to extend data center moratorium to December 16, 2025. County developing tiered ordinance with categories based on square footage and power demand.

event_title: DeKalb County Approves Initial 100-Day Data Center Moratorium
event_description: DeKalb County commissioners approved initial 100-day moratorium on data center applications. First-of-its-kind tiered ordinance in development with categories based on square footage and power demand.

event_title: 1 Million Sq Ft Data Center Campus Proposed for Southwest DeKalb
event_description: Developer proposed 1 million square foot data center campus in southwest DeKalb County. Proposal prompted county to consider moratorium and begin developing tiered ordinance framework.

event_title: DC BLOX Closes $1.15B Green Loan for Atlanta West Campus
event_description: DC BLOX announced closure of $1.15 billion in green loan financing for Atlanta West data center campus in Lithia Springs. Campus spans 100 acres with 120MW capacity expandable to 200MW. Greystone Power Cooperative is utility provider.

event_title: Douglas County Extends Data Center Moratorium 90 Days
event_description: Douglas County commissioners voted to extend 90-day moratorium on data centers for an additional 90 days to continue studying alignment with comprehensive plan.

event_title: Douglas County Approves 90-Day Data Center Moratorium 4-1
event_description: Douglas County Commission approved 90-day moratorium on data centers in 4-1 vote. Commissioner Martin Raxton stated it's an opportunity to look at comprehensive plan and ensure alignment with future vision. Prompted by application for 11 buildings and three warehouse data centers exceeding three times the size of Mall of Georgia.

event_title: Amazon AWS $11B Investment Includes Douglas County
event_description: Amazon Web Services announced $11 billion investment (combined with Butts County) to expand cloud computing and AI infrastructure. Investment expected to create 550+ high-skilled jobs across both counties.

event_title: Microsoft Begins Development on ~1M Sq Ft Douglasville Campus
event_description: Microsoft developing approximately 1 million sq ft data center campus with four 245,000 sq ft technology facilities on 160-acre parcel at 1601 North River Road in Douglasville. Phase I construction began 2024, expected completion 2026.

event_title: Google Data Center Becomes Operational - First in Georgia
event_description: Google's Douglas County data center became operational in 2008, making it one of the first major data centers in Georgia and establishing the region as a data center hub.

event_title: QTS Project Excalibur Construction Begins on 615-Acre Campus
event_description: Construction started on QTS Project Excalibur, described as world's largest multi-tenant data center campus. The 615-acre site will include up to 16 buildings totaling 6.6 million sq ft with $1B+ investment. Full buildout expected by 2032.

event_title: Fayette County Development Authority Sells 615 Acres to QTS for $154M
event_description: Fayette County Development Authority sold 615 acres of farmland west of downtown Fayetteville to QTS for approximately $154 million (~$250,000/acre). Site located at northwest corner of GA Highway 54 and Veterans Parkway.

event_title: Residents Oppose Georgia Power Transmission Line Routes for QTS Campus
event_description: Residents including Diana Dietz raised concerns about Georgia Power transmission line routes through neighborhoods to supply QTS Project Excalibur. Opposition focused on eminent domain concerns and impact on residential areas.

event_title: City of Atlanta Unanimously Approves Special-Use Permit Requirement for Data Centers
event_description: Atlanta City Council unanimously approved requirement for special-use permits for data center development. Effectively bans data centers in neighborhoods including Little Five Points, East Atlanta Village, Inman Park, Virginia-Highlands, and Cascade Heights.

event_title: City of Atlanta Approves Half-Mile Beltline Data Center Ban
event_description: City of Atlanta approved ordinance banning data center development within half-mile radius of the Atlanta Beltline trail system.

event_title: T5 Atlanta IV Acquires 91-Acre Site in South Fulton
event_description: T5 Data Centers finalized acquisition of 91-acre site in South Fulton County for T5 Atlanta IV campus. Project will support 200MW of critical IT load with three buildings totaling 1.32 million sq ft. On-site electrical substation, utility service expected 2026, Phase 1 delivery 2027.

event_title: Microsoft $420M Bond Approved for $1.8B Palmetto Campus
event_description: Development authority approved $420 million bond for Microsoft's $1.8 billion data center campus in Union City/Palmetto area of South Fulton.

event_title: Black Community Organizing Against Data Center Proliferation in South Fulton
event_description: Black community members in South Fulton began organizing against rapid data center development. South Fulton has seen 20+ data centers planned or proposed, including 7 approved in 2024 alone. Concerns about environmental justice and community impact.

event_title: QTS Suwanee 1 DC2 Expansion Adds 30MW Capacity
event_description: QTS completed expansion of Suwanee campus with DC2 adding 30MW capacity and 6 data halls to existing 370K sq ft, 100+MW facility on 53-acre campus.

event_title: Hampton Approves First Data Center in Henry County 5-0
event_description: Hampton City Council approved conditional use permit for Henry County's first data center in unanimous 5-0 vote. Southeast Property Holdings will build three 195K sq ft buildings on 133 acres at Henderson Farms mixed-use development. Includes electrical substation. $400M investment, 650 construction jobs, 90 permanent jobs projected.

event_title: Henry County Data Center Town Hall Held
event_description: Henry County officials held town hall to discuss data center development including pending proposals for Rocky Creek Road (1.2M sq ft) and Simpson Mill Road (1.25M sq ft).

event_title: Zoning Board Reviews Two Data Center Proposals
event_description: Henry County Zoning Board recommended approval for Rocky Creek Road data center (1.2M sq ft) and denial for Simpson Mill Road data center (1.25M sq ft). Final decisions pending Board of Commissioners vote.

event_title: Lamar County Approves Moratorium to Update Zoning Codes
event_description: Lamar County approved moratorium to update commercial and industrial zoning codes that had not been revised since 2010. Planning director Anita Buice noted moratorium was not specifically to block data centers but for general zoning modernization.

event_title: Amazon AWS Purchases 985 Acres in Lamar County for $270M
event_description: Amazon Web Services purchased 985 acres at Legacy 75 Trade Center industrial park along I-75 for approximately $270 million. Property is part of proposed 19 million sq ft development. Amazon spokesperson confirmed site being evaluated for data center development.

event_title: Newton County Technology Park $5B Proposal Filed by TPA Group
event_description: TPA Group filed proposal for Newton County Technology Park, a $5 billion, 317-acre data center campus with 9 buildings totaling 2.6 million sq ft.

event_title: NYT Investigation Documents Water Issues Near Meta Stanton Springs
event_description: New York Times investigation documented water issues in areas near Meta Stanton Springs data center including well failures and sediment buildup in nearby homes.

event_title: Meta Stanton Springs Data Center Becomes Operational
event_description: Meta's Stanton Springs Data Center became operational, spanning 1,000 acres with 8 buildings. Investment exceeded $1 billion. Meta provides $4.5M+ in annual community grants to Newton, Walton, Morgan, and Jasper counties.

event_title: Pike County Approves Data Center Moratorium
event_description: Pike County approved moratorium on data centers. Commissioner James Jenkins stated: 'People just don't understand (data centers) yet. And I motioned a moratorium because it would create a better understanding of how to accommodate (data centers).' Ordinance development underway.

event_title: EPD Permit Review for DC BLOX Wetland and Stream Impacts
event_description: Georgia Environmental Protection Division conducted permit review for DC BLOX Atlanta East campus regarding wetland and stream impacts during November-December 2025.

event_title: DC BLOX Breaks Ground on 216MW Atlanta East Campus
event_description: DC BLOX officially broke ground on Atlanta East hyperscale data center campus in Conyers. Project spans 72 acres with 750K sq ft and 216MW capacity. Phase 1 (160K sq ft) due Q4 2025. Investment estimated at $800M-$1B.

event_title: DC BLOX Receives Incentives from Development Authority of Rockdale County
event_description: Development Authority of Rockdale County granted incentives to DC BLOX through Conyers Rockdale Economic Development Council for Atlanta East data center campus. Chairman Dr. Stephen Bovle stated DC BLOX meets goals for thoughtful and impactful growth.

event_title: Social Circle Area Reaches 7 Data Center Projects Zoned
event_description: Social Circle area spanning Walton and Newton counties reached total of 7 data center projects zoned. Area benefits from Meta Stanton Springs presence and infrastructure.

event_title: Huffaker Road Property Rezoned to Heavy Industrial
event_description: The Rome-Floyd County Development Authority began working with property owner Floyd County 118 LLC to rezone the 347-acre Huffaker Road property as Heavy Industrial in preparation for data center development. This laid the groundwork for the subsequent Microsoft announcement.

event_title: Microsoft Announces $1B Project Firecracker Data Center
event_description: Microsoft announced a $1 billion investment in a data center campus on 347 acres off Huffaker Road during a Rome-Floyd County Development Authority meeting. The project, dubbed Project Firecracker, will purchase land at $40,000 per acre. Microsoft pledged to cover all infrastructure costs and committed to community engagement.

event_title: Microsoft Granted 12-Year Tax Abatement for Project Firecracker
event_description: The Rome-Floyd County Development Authority approved industrial revenue bonds and a 12-year partial tax abatement for Microsoft's Project Firecracker. The abatement covers buildings and equipment, while Microsoft will pay property taxes and county school taxes on the increased land value. Equipment receives a 9-year abatement.

event_title: Floyd County Board of Education Approves Coosa HS Land Sale
event_description: The Floyd County Board of Education approved the sale of 114 acres of property behind Coosa High School through the development authority for data center development. Superintendent Glenn White said the school system had no plans for the property and selling it returns it to the tax rolls.

event_title: RFCDA Approves Option for 114-Acre Coosa HS Data Center Site
event_description: The Rome-Floyd County Development Authority approved an option on 114 acres behind Coosa High School at $40,000 per acre for a data center developer. The buyer is the revocable living trust of William Darryl Edwards, represented by developers Darryl Edwards, Darren Hardin, and Jonathan Ward. The deed restricts use to data center development only.

event_title: RFCDA Approves Land Option for Project Sassy Near Lowe's
event_description: The Rome-Floyd County Development Authority approved an option for 15 acres of property next to the Lowe's Distribution Center for Project Sassy at $60,000 per acre. The 18-month option allows developers to add this land to the adjacent 178-acre site. Developers wanted the option secured before potential 2025 legislation changes.

event_title: Atlas Development Announces Project Sassy for 178-Acre Site
event_description: Atlas Development announced plans for Project Sassy (also known as Dixon Data Center), a 2.49 million square foot data center campus on 178 acres between Plainville Road and Ga. 53 near the Gordon County line. The project would include seven buildings totaling 504MW capacity, with an electrical substation and on-site water cooling systems.

event_title: Project Sassy Rezoning Application Withdrawn
event_description: Atlas Development withdrew its rezoning application for the 178-acre Dixon Data Center (Project Sassy) site on Plainville Road prior to the Rome-Floyd Planning Commission meeting. According to Planning Director Brice Wood, the attorney for the applicant contacted him the day of the meeting requesting withdrawal. Residents had expressed concerns about noise, water usage, and lack of jobs.

event_title: Atlas Development Files DRI for Project Gracie Data Center
event_description: Atlas Development filed a Development of Regional Impact application for Project Gracie, a 2.4 million square foot data center campus on over 200 acres off Vann Road near Coosa Middle School. The seven-building complex has a target completion date of December 2032 and would be developed in phases.

event_title: Planning Commission Recommends Project Gracie Approval 5-2
event_description: The Rome-Floyd County Planning Commission voted 5-2 to recommend approval of the rezoning for Project Gracie. Conditions include limiting use to data centers only, dark-sky lighting requirements, and noise limits of 65 decibels during the day and 55 decibels at night. Superintendent Glenn White spoke in support of the project.

event_title: Residents Pack Hearing to Oppose Project Gracie Data Center
event_description: A packed chamber of Floyd County citizens expressed opposition to the proposed data center near Coosa High School during a public hearing. Residents raised concerns about water and power usage, noise, light pollution, and impacts to quality of life. Speaking time was extended from 10 to 20 minutes per side due to the number of attendees.

event_title: Floyd County Commission Unanimously Approves Project Gracie Rezoning
event_description: Despite significant community opposition, the Floyd County Commission unanimously approved (4-0) the rezoning for Atlas Development's Project Gracie data center. Conditions include: use limited to data centers, dark-sky lighting, 65/55 decibel noise limits, 100-foot undisturbed setback, and sound study requirements with fines up to $1,000/day for violations.

event_title: Development Authority Approves Battey Business Complex Sale to Atlas
event_description: The Rome-Floyd County Development Authority approved the sale of property in the Battey Business Complex (former Northwest Georgia Regional Hospital site) to Atlas Development for a data center. Atlas will pay $50,000 per acre totaling $5.7 million with $150,000 earnest money. A 19-month due diligence period allows for asbestos remediation before closing.

event_title: Digital Realty Data Center Campus Approved at Fort Gillem
event_description: Digital Realty received approval to construct a data center campus within Forest Park city limits at the former Fort Gillem site. This project, along with the TA Realty project in Ellenwood, comprised the two data center approvals in Clayton County preceding the 2025 moratorium.

event_title: QTS Signs 350 MW Renewable Energy Agreement with Georgia Power
event_description: QTS Realty Trust signed a 20-year agreement with Georgia Power to procure nearly 350 megawatts of renewable energy. Once active, this deal supplies about 90 percent of the electricity used at QTS's Atlanta-Metro and Suwanee data center campuses from renewable sources. The agreement supports QTS's sustainability goals.

event_title: Northern Data Announces 120MW HPC Data Center in Maysville
event_description: Northern Data Group announced plans for an AI and HPC-focused data center on a 63-acre site in Maysville, spanning Banks and Jackson counties approximately 70 miles northeast of Atlanta. The facility will deliver 120MW with capacity to expand to 180MW. Design has begun and the data center is expected to be fully operational in Q1 2027. The site will support high-density and liquid-cooled infrastructure.

event_title: Northern Data 120MW Data Center Spans Banks County
event_description: The Northern Data Group data center in Maysville spans both Banks and Jackson counties. The 63-acre site will deliver 120MW with potential expansion to 180MW. Maysville City Council Representative Kim Wilmoth expressed enthusiasm for the project, noting franchise fees for power will support city expenditures.

event_title: Georgia DCA Adopts New Data Center Review Process at Savannah Meeting
event_description: The Georgia Department of Community Affairs board unanimously approved new rules expanding Development of Regional Impact reviews to explicitly include data centers at its quarterly meeting in Savannah. The addition of a 'technological facilities' category was needed because DCA's 12 regional councils lacked agreement on how to treat data centers. This followed DCA's July 2025 temporary pause on state reviews of data center DRI proposals.

event_title: State Water Subcommittee Holds Meeting in Moultrie Discussing Data Center Impacts
event_description: A Georgia House water subcommittee meeting was held in Moultrie where Rep. Robert Dickey raised concerns about large industrial facilities like data centers competing with agriculture for water resources. Dickey asked who would make decisions allowing large industrial facilities while potentially leaving agriculture 'high and dry' with limited water supply. The meeting was part of broader state-level discussions about data center resource impacts.

event_title: Project Azalea Data Center DRI Filed in McDuffie County
event_description: A Development of Regional Impact application was filed for Project Azalea, a data center campus in McDuffie County. The project would include up to six data center buildings on 200 acres at 2660-2358 Randall Hunt Road in Thomson, near a large electrical substation. The project could be completed by 2029. Public comments can be submitted to projectazaleacomments@thomson-mcduffie.gov.

event_title: Grantville Approves Zoning Change to Allow Data Centers
event_description: Grantville City Council voted 4-1 to update zoning language to add 'data center' as a special use permit option within certain zones. Mayor Richard Proctor has identified a 196-acre property near I-85 and U.S. 29 as ideal for data center development. A 'Grantville against Data Centers' Facebook group formed with 166 members following the meeting. Councilwoman Dee Berry raised concerns about noise and water supply.

event_title: Covington Enacts 180-Day Data Center Moratorium
event_description: The Covington City Council implemented a 180-day moratorium on new data center requests. Council Member Travis Moore proposed the ordinance revision to change 'by right' allowances in the current ordinance. The current ordinance (implemented September 2023) allows data centers in M1/M2 zones by right. During the moratorium, staff will review the ordinance and offer recommendations.

event_title: Georgia PSC Unanimously Approves $16B Power Expansion for Data Centers
event_description: The Georgia Public Service Commission voted 5-0 to approve Georgia Power's request for 9,885 MW of new energy capacity, the largest expansion in state history. The plan includes five new natural gas plants at Plant Bowen (Bartow), Plant McIntosh (Effingham), and Plant Wansley (Heard/Carroll). Total cost estimated at $16B+ for utility-owned generation. Protesters disrupted the vote chanting 'The people say nay!' Critics argue only 0.22% probability the projections materialize.

event_title: Rep. Romman Introduces Statewide Data Center Moratorium Bill
event_description: Democratic state Rep. Ruwa Romman introduced legislation that would place a moratorium on new data center construction through 2027. Romman said she recruited Republican co-sponsors and described the effort as bipartisan. The bill faces opposition from Rep. Brad Thomas who said a statewide moratorium 'goes too far' and could choke off economic growth.

event_title: Microsoft Fairwater AI Data Center Opens at QTS Campus
event_description: Microsoft's Fairwater AI data center began operations at the QTS Fayetteville campus. The facility is a two-story design using closed-loop liquid cooling that 'consumes almost zero water.' It houses hundreds of thousands of Nvidia GB200 and GB300 GPUs (up to 72 per rack). Microsoft forewent on-site UPS and generators due to reliable grid. CEO Satya Nadella announced it as part of 'the world's first AI superfactory.'

event_title: QTS Files DRI for ATL2 East 313-Acre Expansion
event_description: QTS (via QTS Eastwood LLC) filed a Development of Regional Impact application for ATL2 East, a 2 million sq ft data center on approximately 313 acres west of Veterans Parkway in Fayetteville. This expands the campus from 615 acres to 900 acres. The project could be completed by 2029. QTS is expected to become one of Fayette County's largest taxpayers, potentially exceeding $40M annually.

event_title: Wallace Jackson $3.7B Data Center Campus DRI Filed
event_description: Wallace Jackson LLC filed a DRI application for a 4.986 million sq ft data center campus on 189 acres in the Wallace Jackson Industrial Park on Jackson Road. The $3.7B project would include 10 buildings with full build-out by 2035. This is the third major data center proposed for Spalding County, following approvals of Spalding Investments LLC (8 buildings, 127 acres) and Montana Property Group's 'Project Spalding' (2.55M sq ft).

event_title: Crawford County Passes 6-Month Data Center Moratorium
event_description: Crawford County Commissioners unanimously passed (5-0) a 180-day moratorium on data center permits on January 6, 2026. Planning & Zoning originally voted on the moratorium at their December 18, 2025 meeting. County attorney Joel Sherlock stated the county lacks infrastructure and procedures for data center applications. A public work session was scheduled for January 20, 2026 in Roberta. No data center has been proposed for the county; this is a preventive measure.

event_title: Griffin City Council Passes 180-Day Data Center Moratorium
event_description: The Griffin City Council unanimously (7-0) passed a 180-day moratorium on data center permitting, applications, and cryptocurrency mining operations until mid-July 2026. The resolution allows city planning staff to study current codes and review how other metro Atlanta jurisdictions have approached data center regulations. The city's UDC currently does not specifically allow 'Technological Facilities' either by right or special use permit. Staff will make recommendations for UDC revisions.

event_title: Columbia County Creates DC Data Center Zoning District
event_description: Columbia County Board of Commissioners approved Ordinance No. 25-07, creating new DC data-center district and amending Chapter 90. Key provisions: 70 dB noise limit at property line, 500-ft buffer from residential (reducible to 250 ft with berm), 250-ft buffer from roads, no private wells permitted, generator testing restricted to minimize noise. Residents criticized 70 dB limit as too high.

event_title: Columbia County Planning Commission Hears Three Data Center Proposals
event_description: Four-and-a-half-hour meeting with approximately 50 public comments on three data center proposals near I-20 Exit 183: White Oak (29 buildings, 3,100 acres), Byrd Farm (18 buildings, 944 acres), and Pumpkin Center. Many residents opposed, wanting retail development instead. Planning Commission recommended approval despite opposition.
project_name: White Oak, Byrd Farm, Pumpkin Center

event_title: Residents Sue Twiggs County Over Data Center Approval
event_description: Group of Twiggs County residents filed lawsuit in Superior Court alleging county ignored zoning rules and public notice requirements when approving Pine Ridge Tech Park on September 18, 2025. Lawsuit claims sign was posted on wrong property and listed incorrect hearing date. Plaintiffs also allege failure to evaluate utility impacts, black bear population, and Muscogee Nation sacred land status.

event_title: Twiggs County Files Response to Lawsuit
event_description: In county's December response to resident lawsuit, Twiggs County denied claims that rezoning decision was made in haste or resulted from fraud, corruption, or manifest abuse. County also denied that plaintiffs have substantial interest in zoning decision or will suffer permanent injury.

event_title: Trammell Crow Proposes $21B Forsyth Technology Campus in City of Forsyth
event_description: CBRE's Trammell Crow Company filed DRI application for Forsyth Technology Campus, a $21B, 12 million sq ft data center campus on 1,632 acres between Georgia Public Safety Training Center and Johnstonville Road. Up to 21 buildings planned with 165-230 employees. 200-ft natural buffer on western/northern borders, sound blankets and absorbing walls planned. Third major data center proposal in Monroe County.

event_title: Henry County Holds First Public Hearing on Data Center Ordinance
event_description: Henry County Board of Commissioners held first of two public hearings on proposed data center ordinance. Key provisions: M-1/M-2 zoning only, conditional use permit required, 200-ft landscape buffer, 500-ft setback from non-industrial zoning, 1,000-ft setback from residential, 30% open space preservation, development agreement required addressing noise, water, public safety, environmental reviews. No moratorium adopted.

event_title: Haynes Station Residents Raise Concerns About Project Eisenhower Process
event_description: Residents from Haynes Station subdivision brought concerns about Project Eisenhower to Augusta Commission, questioning how governing body cut through red tape on project dating to 2022. Dr. Zakiya Mabrey cited process concerns. Commissioner Catherine Smith-Rice proposed public meeting with citizens, which Mayor Garnett Johnson agreed to.

event_title: Multiple Data Center Bills Filed in Georgia Legislature 2026 Session
event_description: Seven data center bills filed in 2026 session: HB 1012 (statewide moratorium until March 2027 - Rep.
