Romman), HB 559 (end sales tax break Dec 2026), SB 34 (protect residential customers from DC electricity costs - advancing through committee). Other bills would require public disclosure of water/electricity usage. Senate Finance Chairman Hufstetler supports SB 34.

event_title: DeKalb County Defers Data Center Ordinance Vote
event_description: DeKalb County Commission held public hearing on proposed data center ordinance but deferred vote on regulations. Moratorium remains in effect until June 23, 2026. Proposed ordinance creates first-of-its-kind tiered categories based on square footage and power demand. Major/campus DCs limited to M and M-2 zones with Special Land Use Permit. 500-ft buffer from residential and parks, closed-loop water required, noise/water/energy assessments required. Residents raised health and cost concerns at hearing.

event_title: Spalding County Planning Commission Special Meeting on Wallace Jackson Data Center
event_description: Spalding County Planning and Appeals Commission held special called meeting to hear variance, zoning, and special exception applications for Wallace Jackson Data Center Campus. The $3.7B project would include 10 data center buildings totaling 4.986 million sq ft on 189 acres in Wallace Jackson Industrial Park.

event_title: Spalding County Approves Wallace Jackson $3.9B Data Center Campus Unanimously
event_description: Spalding County Commissioners voted unanimously to approve the Wallace Jackson LLC data center campus, a $3.9B, 5 million sq ft project spanning 190 acres along I-75. The approval came despite protests from dozens of residents who cited environmental pollution concerns and loss of generational agricultural land. Officials claim the project will lower resident tax burdens. The 10-building complex is the third major data center approved for Spalding County, joining Spalding Investments LLC and Project Spalding approvals from 2025. Construction timeline not yet determined.

event_title: Coweta County Adopts Data Center Ordinance After Months of Debate
event_description: Coweta County Board of Commissioners adopted data center ordinance in 4-1 vote (Commissioner Bill McKenzie dissenting). Key provisions: 300-foot buffer from residential, open-loop cooling prohibited, closed-loop water systems required, waste management plan and annual reports required. Moratorium expired December 17, 2025. Ordinance allows Project Sail and other pending projects to proceed under new rules.

event_title: City of Roswell Enacts Data Center Moratorium
event_description: City of Roswell enacted moratorium on new data centers, joining approximately a dozen other Georgia municipalities with similar restrictions. Moratorium set to expire April 12, 2026. Roswell joins Atlanta, Peachtree City, LaGrange, Social Circle, and others in restricting data center development.

event_title: Forsyth City Council Approves $21B Forsyth Technology Campus
event_description: City of Forsyth leaders approved special conditional rezoning for the Forsyth Technology Campus, overriding objections from residents and the planning/zoning board recommendation (which ended in 3-3 tie). The $21B, 12 million sq ft Trammell Crow development is projected to generate $224 million in annual tax revenue and create 165-230 permanent jobs. Project will quintuple city's tax base. Monroe County's separate moratorium does not apply to city property.

event_title: Columbia County Approves Two Data Centers and Denies One
event_description: Columbia County commissioners voted to approve two data center projects (Pumpkin Center and White Oak) and denied the Byrd Farm project due to inability to identify an end user. The approvals follow the January 21 Planning Commission hearing where all three were recommended for approval despite significant resident opposition.

event_title: Atlas Development Files Project Bus for 350-Acre Data Center Campus in Temple
event_description: Atlas Development LLC filed Project Bus, a proposed 350-acre data center campus on Center Point Road in Temple, approximately 40 miles west of Atlanta. The project envisions up to 12 buildings and 2 substations with an estimated investment of $11 billion at full build-out, potentially completed by 2036. More than a dozen residents spoke against the project at commission meetings, citing energy and water consumption, disruption of rural life, and property value impacts.

event_title: Local Environmental Groups Release Data Center Recommendations
event_description: Local environmental groups in Athens-Clarke County released recommendations for data center rules as the Planning Commission considers drafted regulations. Athens-Clarke County has a moratorium in effect through March 6, 2026.

event_title: Cielo Digital Infrastructure Announces $2.1B Cherokee County Data Center
event_description: Cielo Digital Infrastructure announced a $2.1 billion data center on Ford Road in Cherokee County. The project represents a major hyperscale investment in the county.

event_title: Marietta Approves 347K SF Data Center Campus Rezoning
event_description: Marietta City Council approved rezoning for a 347,200 square foot data center campus at 1751 Bells Ferry Road. The 108MW facility represents significant investment in Cobb County.

event_title: Gordon County Enacts Preemptive Data Center Moratorium
event_description: Gordon County enacted a preemptive data center moratorium while studying regulations for potential data center development. The moratorium was passed before any formal proposals were submitted.

event_title: Atlas Development Proposes 2M SF Dixon Data Center in Gordon County
event_description: Atlas Development Inc. filed rezoning request for Dixon Data Center campus on 178 acres near Ga. 53 in Gordon County. The proposed 2 million square foot complex would be a major development for the area.

event_title: Permit Approved for Ringgold Data Center Campus
event_description: Catoosa County approved permit for Ringgold data center campus in November 2024.

event_title: Fayetteville Passes 90-Day Data Center Moratorium
event_description: Fayetteville City Council passed a 90-day moratorium on data center development applications. Projects already in review are not affected. City Attorney Patrick Jaugstetter stated the council could pursue an extension if the city hasn't completed updating its Unified Development Ordinance within that timeframe. The moratorium allows time to update development regulations and address community concerns regarding resource use and infrastructure impacts.

event_title: Fayetteville Planning Commission Denies CHI/Acquisitions Data Center 3-2
event_description: Fayetteville Planning and Zoning Commission voted 3-2 to deny conceptual site plan for the 'Hwy 85 N DC Project' proposed by CHI/Acquisitions, LP on Highway 85 North. Approximately 100 residents filled the meeting room in opposition. The property is zoned Business Park (BP) which allows data centers as permitted use, so decision is advisory. Final authority rests with City Council. Denial based on site design concerns and community opposition regarding 'mammoth utility poles.' Developer has appealed to City Council with hearing scheduled March 19, 2026.

event_title: QTS Unveils Multi-Use Path as Community Partnership Effort
event_description: QTS unveiled a 3,000-foot multi-use path segment on the southern edge of its Fayetteville property designed to connect to existing local trail infrastructure. This represents QTS's response to community criticism and is part of expanding community partnership efforts toward building a countywide cart path network.

event_title: Georgia Power Transmission Line Installation Sparks Resident Opposition
event_description: Georgia Power using eminent domain to install nearly 200-foot tall transmission line poles across Fayette County to power QTS data center. Over 330 parcels affected by the Ashley Park-Wansley project spanning Coweta, Fayette, Fulton, and Heard counties. 21 homes slated for acquisition. Community concerns include property value reduction, forest clear-cutting, and visual impact on Hopeful Baptist Church (established 1825). Resident Diana Dietz has led bus tours for 3+ years educating community about environmental and infrastructure impacts. Project need date: June 1, 2029.

event_title: Environmental Groups Challenge Georgia Power Data Center Expansion at PSC Hearing
event_description: Georgia Public Service Commission held hearings on Georgia Power's data center power expansion plan February 12-13. Environmental groups and customers testified against the plan, arguing that regulators failed to prove all 10 GW of new capacity was needed. Groups challenged the December 2025 approval of the $16B expansion including five new natural gas plants.

event_title: Henry County Brings Data Center Ordinance Back for February Vote
event_description: Henry County Board of Commissioners directed staff to modify proposed data center ordinance and bring revised version back for vote in February 2026. The ordinance establishes zoning restrictions (M-1/M-2 only), conditional use permits, 1,000-foot residential setbacks, 200-foot landscape buffers, and 30% open space preservation requirements. This follows the January 6 first public hearing.

event_title: Richmond County Residents Hold Belair Elementary Hearing on Project Eisenhower
event_description: Richmond County residents held hearing at Belair Elementary to voice objections to the proposed Project Eisenhower data center in Haynes Station neighborhood. Dr. Zakiya Mabrey and other residents testified about environmental and community concerns. This follows the January 14 Augusta Commission meeting where residents first raised process concerns.

event_title: Additional Data Center Bills Advance in Georgia Legislature
event_description: Multiple data center bills advancing in 2026 session beyond previously reported HB 1012 and SB 34: SB 410 (ban new tax exemptions), SB 408/HB 559 (sunset existing exemptions), HB 528 (water/electricity reporting requirements), SB 421 (local government disclosure requirements), HB 1063 (ensure fossil fuel plant costs borne by data centers not residential customers).

event_title: Putnam County Board of Commissioners Approves Rezoning Moratorium
event_description: Putnam County Board of Commissioners approved up to six-month moratorium on all new rezoning applications, effective September 16, 2025 through March 16, 2026. Moratorium passed during statewide wave of data center regulation efforts.

event_title: Putnam County Partially Lifts Rezoning Moratorium
event_description: Putnam County partially lifted its rezoning moratorium. Areas south of Highway 16 and west of Highway 441 are no longer under moratorium. Moratorium remains in effect for areas north of Highway 16 and east of Highway 441 until March 16, 2026.

event_title: Atlas Development Files DRI for $11B Project Bus Data Center Campus
event_description: Atlas Development LLC filed Development of Regional Impact application for Project Bus, a 350-acre data center campus with 12 buildings and 2 substations in Temple. $11 billion investment at full build-out by 2036. Estimated $42.5 million annual tax revenue. Temple straddles Haralson and Carroll counties.

event_title: Atlas Development Withdraws Project Bus Following Community Opposition
event_description: Atlas Development withdrew Project Bus data center proposal following community concerns about energy and water consumption. Developer retains option to resubmit with modifications. The 350-acre, $11B project had faced pushback from residents.

event_title: Red Wolf Properties Files DRI for Project Splice in Crisp County
event_description: Red Wolf Properties filed Development of Regional Impact (DRI) application with Georgia Department of Community Affairs for Project Splice, a 2.1 million sq ft technology campus on 583 acres outside Cordele. $6 billion investment with phases completing 2029-2033. Expected 180-200 permanent jobs plus 270 ancillary positions.

event_title: Georgia Senate Passes HB 134 Tax Reform Repealing Data Center Exemptions
event_description: Georgia Senate passed HB 134, a comprehensive tax reform bill reducing personal and corporate income tax rates while repealing the ability to grant new sales and use tax exemptions for data centers. Bill returns to Georgia House for concurrence on Senate amendments.

event_title: New Data Center Bills Filed: SB 436 HB 1059 and SB 476
event_description: Three additional data center bills filed: SB 436 (Sen. Jaha Howard) suspends new sales tax exemptions July 2026-June 2027 and prohibits local government NDAs on water/electricity usage; HB 1059 (Rep. Derrick Jackson of Tyrone) creates moratorium July 2026-Dec 2028 and establishes 14-member Data Center Impact Commission with 3-year study; SB 476 (Sen. Blake Tillery) comprehensive tax reform repealing DC exemptions.

event_title: Georgia PSC Rejects Motion to Reconsider Data Center Power Expansion 3-2
event_description: Georgia Public Service Commission voted 3-2 to reject motion from environmental groups (Sierra Club, Southern Environmental Law Center, Southern Alliance for Clean Energy) to reconsider its December 19 approval of Georgia Power's 10 GW expansion plan. Republicans Shaw, Pridemore, and McDonald voted against reconsideration; Democrats Hubbard and Johnson voted for it. The $50-60 billion expansion plan remains approved.

event_title: Hampton Technology Park DRI Filed for 603-Acre 4M SF Data Center Campus
event_description: Hampton Technology Park Owner LLC filed a Development of Regional Impact (DRI) application with Georgia Department of Community Affairs for a 603-acre data center campus in the City of Hampton. The project could total 5 buildings and 4 million square feet, making it one of the largest proposed campuses in Georgia.

event_title: Newton County Commission Approves 30-Day Emergency Data Center Moratorium
event_description: Newton County Commission unanimously approved a 30-day emergency moratorium on data center permitting, separate from the City of Covington's existing 180-day moratorium. County staff directed to work on text amendments and update Unified Development Ordinance (UDO) language during the moratorium period.

event_title: Walton County Approves 1.78M SF Data Center Annexation Near Social Circle
event_description: Walton County commissioners unanimously approved annexation for a 1.78 million square foot data center at Amber Stapp Studdard Road near Social Circle. The four-building facility adds to the growing cluster of data centers in the Social Circle corridor.

event_title: Social Circle Approves Sailfish Investors 1.8M SF Data Center
event_description: Social Circle City Council approved annexation, rezoning, and special-use permit for Sailfish Investors' 1.8 million square foot four-building data center facility. This follows the initial Sailfish annexation approval in December 2024.

event_title: Judge to Decide Whether Weyerhaeuser Remains Defendant in Twiggs Data Center Lawsuit
event_description: Court hearing held to determine whether Weyerhaeuser (property owner) should remain as a defendant in the residents' lawsuit challenging Twiggs County's $2 billion data center approval. Residents allege improper notice, missing environmental review (DRI), failure to assess wildlife and cultural impacts. County allegedly placed rezoning sign on wrong property.

event_title: Lowndes County Approves 719-Acre Data Center Rezoning Unanimously
event_description: Lowndes County Commission unanimously approved rezoning of approximately 719 acres on Coleman Road off North Valdosta Road from C-C/R-1/CON to M-1/CON for data center development (REZ-2025-11). Property owner Pope Langdale (Langdale Capital Assets) partnered with DC BLOX. Project projected to create 400 jobs at $135k average salary. Approximately 40 residents signed petition opposing rezoning. Francesca Theres represented opposition.

event_title: Lowndes County Data Center Town Hall Draws Opposition at VSU
event_description: Town hall held at VSU Student Union Theater organized by Lowndes Citizens Against Data Centers, Alpha Kappa Alpha Sorority, and VSU Anthropology Club. Speakers included Amy Sharma (Science for Georgia) and Hannah Baker (Sierra Club Georgia). Baker called for moratorium. Residents voiced concerns about water consumption, utility rates, environmental impacts. Community debate intensified after July 2025 rezoning approval.

event_title: Georgia Senate Adjourns to Avoid Vote on Weakened SB 34 Data Center Bill
event_description: Georgia Senate abruptly adjourned just before voting on SB 34, the data center consumer protection bill. Democratic Minority Leader Harold Jones said Republicans lacked votes to defeat amendments restoring stronger consumer protections. The adjournment effectively stalled the most prominent data center bill with crossover day (March 6) approaching. Bill sponsor Hufstetler opposed the weakened substitute.

event_title: Cobb County Approves 180-Day Data Center Moratorium Unanimously
event_description: Cobb County Board of Commissioners voted unanimously to approve a 180-day temporary moratorium on new data center applications in unincorporated areas. Commissioners cited concerns about noise pollution, air quality, water consumption (1+ million gallons/day), and power demand. Moratorium allows county to study infrastructure and environmental impacts.

event_title: Bulloch County Approves 90-Day Data Center Moratorium Unanimously
event_description: Bulloch County Commissioners unanimously approved a 90-day moratorium on data center permitting in unincorporated areas. Followed by work session with Georgia Power representatives to discuss infrastructure capacity.

event_title: Columbus City Council Discusses $5.18B Project Ruby Data Center
event_description: Columbus City Council meeting discussed Project Ruby, a proposed $5.18 billion data center on approximately 900 acres in northeast Muscogee County. Project would create 195 jobs ($80K-$120K salaries) and demand 600 megawatts of power (exceeding Columbus's entire current resource needs) and 90,000-260,000 gallons of water daily. Multiple approval steps required; next meeting March 6, 2026.

event_title: Athens-Clarke County Commissioners Discuss Outright Data Center Ban
event_description: Athens-Clarke County commissioners discussed proposals to permanently ban data centers rather than just extending the current moratorium (expiring March 6). Planning commission proposed code amendments classifying data centers as level-three industrial uses, effectively banning them. Commissioner Melissa Link called AI 'an amoral enterprise.' Mayor and commission weighing permanent ban vs. restrictive regulations.

event_title: Columbia County Citizen Files Lawsuits Challenging Data Center Rezoning Decisions
event_description: A Columbia County citizen filed lawsuits challenging the February 3-4 rezoning decisions that approved White Oak Technology Park and Pumpkin Technology Campus data centers. Legal action challenges the validity of the rezoning approvals.

event_title: QTS Holds Town Hall at Belair Elementary on Project Eisenhower Concerns
event_description: QTS Data Centers held town hall meeting at Belair Elementary School to address community concerns about Project Eisenhower. Residents from Haynes Station area raised concerns about project size, traffic, noise, and wetlands impacts. This follows the January resident-led hearing at the same location.

event_title: Irwin County Planning Commission Holds Special Exception Hearing on Data Center
event_description: Irwin County Planning Advisory Commission held special exception hearing for Irwin Forward Data Center/Tech Park on 546.35 acres at Ponderosa Drive and Alapaha River Road. Applicant James Russell Bryant acting for The Marcus D. Fletcher Trust. Project claims closed-loop water system. Neighbors expressed concerns about groundwater depletion, wildlife disruption, and rural land exploitation. Change.org petition 'Protect Irwin County from DATA CENTERS' launched. County also moving to dissolve industrial authority.

event_title: Irwin County Commission Public Hearing Scheduled on Data Center Proposal
event_description: Irwin County Commission public hearing scheduled for March 2, 2026 at 5:45 PM at Irwin County Courthouse on the Irwin Forward Data Center proposal. 546-acre site on agricultural land near the Tift County line. Landowner Marvin Peavy on adjacent Tift County property reported not being contacted about the project.

event_title: Senate Utilities Committee Weakens SB 34 Consumer Protection Bill 9-3
event_description: Georgia Senate Utilities Committee voted 9-3 to approve a substitute version of SB 34 that significantly weakened consumer protections. Original sponsor Sen. Chuck Hufstetler (R-Rome) stated the substitute offers 'no protection to our consumers.' The weakened version incorporated HB 1063 language but stripped stronger safeguards from the original bill.

event_title: Troup County Extends Data Center Moratorium Another 90 Days to June 14
event_description: Troup County Board of Commissioners voted to extend the county-wide data center moratorium for an additional 90 days, from the March 16 expiration to approximately June 14, 2026. The extension provides continued time for the county to develop its data center regulatory framework. Project West, a proposed $9.7 billion campus with 1.5 million sq ft across 6 buildings on 513 acres, remains pending during the moratorium. The City of LaGrange also maintains its own separate moratorium.

event_title: Georgia Crossover Day: HB 1063 Advances to Senate; SB 34 Stalls
event_description: On Georgia's legislative Crossover Day (March 6), HB 1063—which requires electric utilities and new data centers to enter agreements ensuring residential and small-business customers do not bear data center infrastructure costs—cleared the House with 159-5 bipartisan support and crossed to the Senate. SB 34, the stronger consumer protection bill that would have explicitly banned any data center-related costs from appearing on residential electric bills, failed to advance past the crossover deadline after the Senate adjourned abruptly on February 27 before a floor vote. HB 1063 is now the primary legislative vehicle moving forward. Multiple other bills including HB 1012 (statewide moratorium) and HB 1059 (moratorium + study commission) also did not cross over.

event_title: White House Ratepayer Protection Pledge Signed by Major Tech Companies
event_description: Seven major technology companies—Amazon, Google, Meta, Microsoft, OpenAI, Oracle, and xAI—signed the White House Ratepayer Protection Pledge on March 4, committing to build or purchase new power generation sources for their data centers and cover infrastructure costs rather than passing them to residential utility customers. The Sierra Club Georgia Chapter issued a statement on the pledge, noting it aligns with goals of Georgia's SB 34 and HB 1063 but lacks enforcement mechanisms.

event_title: Newton County Extends Data Center Moratorium to April 8
event_description: Newton County Board of Commissioners extended its data center moratorium from the March 18 expiration to April 8, 2026, providing additional time for the Development Services Department to draft revisions to the Unified Development Ordinance. The moratorium covers new data center permitting and applications county-wide. Meta's existing hyperscale data center accounts for roughly 10% of the county's daily water use, and data center development has expanded into incorporated cities including Covington, Social Circle, and Porterdale.

event_title: Polk County Commission Approves Data Center Ordinance
event_description: Polk County Commission voted to approve a new ordinance governing the construction and operations of data centers within the county. The ordinance establishes preemptive regulatory standards in advance of any formal data center proposals. Zoning changes associated with the ordinance are expected to be completed by end of May 2026. This follows the county's earlier consideration of moratorium language in October 2025.

event_title: Monroe County Planning & Zoning Recommends Data Center Ordinance Amendments
event_description: Monroe County Planning and Zoning Board voted 4-0 to recommend amendments to the Unified Development Ordinance that would reclassify data centers from commercial to light industrial zoning and require 500-foot vegetative buffers. The Board of Commissioners is scheduled to vote on adoption March 17 at 9 AM. The county currently has an active moratorium and has seen significant data center interest including Google's 950-acre land purchase and the Rumble Technology Campus (4.2 million sq ft planned on 900+ acres).

event_title: Central Coweta Industrial Phase II $4 Billion Data Center Complex Filed as DRI
event_description: Central Coweta Industrial Phase II (DRI #4374) was submitted as a Development of Regional Impact application proposing a $4 billion data center complex consisting of 8 buildings totaling 2.4 million square feet on 458 acres in central Coweta County. The project is estimated to generate $40 million in annual local tax revenue with completion projected by 2028. This is in addition to the pending Project Sail ($17 billion, 832 acres) and other data center proposals in the county.

event_title: Project Turbo Developers Withdraw Special Use But Pursue LID Rezoning and Annexation
event_description: Williams Brothers Development (Cameron Grogan) withdrew the data center special use permit application but secured light industrial development (LID) zoning for the 119-acre site at 2400 O'Kelly Road. Developers announced they are 'still pursuing' the data center through an alternative pathway: annexation into the City of Gainesville to gain access to city sewer infrastructure, which would allow treated wastewater to be returned to the Chattahoochee River basin. The initial 500,000 gpd water request was revised to 225,000 gpd with a closed-loop cooling system.
outcome: LID zoning approved; annexation path pursued

event_title: Hall County Approves 180-Day Moratorium on Data Centers
event_description: Hall County Board of Commissioners voted 4-0 (District 2 Commissioner Billy Powell absent) to approve a 180-day moratorium on data centers, planned industrial development, and detention centers, effective through approximately August 26, 2026. The moratorium pauses acceptance of new rezoning applications, construction permits, and special use permits for data centers. KEY EXEMPTION: Applications already heard and recommended by the Planning Commission before the moratorium date are NOT affected. However, all other pending applications 'will be deemed withdrawn, with application funds refunded.' NOTE: The Hall County Planning Commission itself was temporarily suspended pending investigation during this period, with the Board of Commissioners hearing applications directly. Chairman David Gibbs stated the moratorium can be extended 'whether it's months or years' after expiration. Properties already zoned light industrial (I-1)—including Project Turbo's 119-acre site—are not automatically exempt from the data center moratorium; data center use in any zone still requires approval that the moratorium pauses.
outcome: Moratorium approved 4-0; exemptions for already-heard applications

event_title: Columbia County Chairman Promotes Homestead Tax Exemption from Data Center Revenue
event_description: Columbia County Commission Chairman Doug Duncan publicly promoted the argument that the White Oak Technology Park data center could generate enough tax revenue to offset all residential property taxes in the county. Duncan stated the county's general fund is about $100 million with $20 million from homestead property taxes, and that even $500 million in data center assessed value would enable a homestead exemption. County officials announced they are 'actively collaborating with state legislators' on House Bill 1156 and House Resolution 1178 to enact homestead tax relief provisions tied to data center revenue. Development Authority Director Cheney Eldridge also promoted the project on WGAC radio. Duncan cautioned benefits 'won't happen right away—it will take several years.'

event_title: Spalding County Officials Frame $3.9B Data Center as Path to Lower Residential Taxes
event_description: During the January 23 vote approving the Wallace Jackson $3.9B data center campus, Spalding County Attorney Steven Ledbetter stated that the 'intent and direction the board is taking is to lower the taxes.' Officials explicitly framed the 190-acre, 10-building, 5M sq ft campus as 'a major win for local taxpayers,' arguing the center will provide a significant economic boost and enable residential property tax relief. This was cited as a primary justification despite dozens of residents protesting environmental concerns and loss of agricultural land.
outcome: Approved unanimously; tax relief argument central to justification

event_title: ACCG Deputy Director Calls Data Centers a 'Cash Cow' for Lowering Residential Property Taxes
event_description: Clint Mueller, Deputy Director of the Association County Commissioners of Georgia (ACCG), stated that 'probably the biggest positive aspect that a lot of county commissioners are looking at is they're trying to lower taxes for their other residents, and they look at this as a sort of a cash cow to do that with.' Mueller estimated a data center investment of ~$125 million per megawatt could yield $6 billion in real and personal property value over 15 years, translating to ~$27 million in annual tax revenue. This reflects a growing statewide narrative among local officials framing data centers as a tool for residential property tax relief.

event_title: Athens-Clarke County Commission Unanimously Extends Data Center Moratorium to June 5
event_description: Athens-Clarke County Commission voted unanimously on March 3 to extend the temporary emergency moratorium on new data center applications from March 6 to June 5, 2026. The extension allows time to finalize proposed zoning amendments that would categorize data centers as Level 3 industrial (highest-impact), require special use permits, mandate closed-loop cooling systems, impose 400-foot property line buffers, require noise barriers, and mandate annual operating reports. Several commissioners continue to explore the legality of an outright data center ban.

event_title: Carroll County Approves 100-Day Moratorium on Data Centers and Related Facilities
event_description: Carroll County Board of Commissioners approved a 100-day moratorium (effective through approximately early June 2026) on data centers, crypto mining facilities, battery energy storage systems (BESS), and solar panel farms in unincorporated Carroll County. The moratorium prohibits acceptance of applications, issuance of land disturbance permits, and other development permits for these facility types. Carroll County Community Development Department was directed not to accept applications or issue permits. County staff and County Attorney directed to review and revise the Carroll County Zoning Ordinance for 'New Technology Facilities and Uses.' NOTE: The moratorium applies only to unincorporated county areas—Villa Rica's approved Avemore project is within city limits and is not affected.

event_title: Georgia Senate Passes SB 410 Repealing Data Center Sales Tax Exemptions
event_description: On Crossover Day (March 6), the Georgia Senate passed SB 410, which repeals state sales and use tax exemptions for data center equipment and requires data centers—not residential customers—to cover the full cost of new generation and transmission infrastructure. The bill was sent to the House for consideration before the session ends in April. This is separate from HB 1063 (which passed the House the same day) and represents the Senate's stronger approach to ending data center tax breaks.

event_title: HB 1116 Property Tax Relief Bill Passes Georgia House 98-68
event_description: House Bill 1116, sponsored by Rep. Shaw Blackmon, passed the Georgia House 98-68 on Crossover Day. The bill caps annual property tax assessment increases at 3% and directs revenue from data centers—starting in 2029 when the current equipment tax exemption expires—toward reducing homestead property taxes. This is the legislative embodiment of the 'data centers will lower your property taxes' argument that counties like Columbia and Spalding have been making at the local level.

event_title: DeKalb County Extends Data Center Moratorium to June 23
event_description: DeKalb County Board of Commissioners voted to extend the data center moratorium to June 23, 2026, deferring adoption of its draft data center ordinance. DeKalb had developed a first-of-its-kind tiered ordinance with categories based on square footage and power demand, addressing noise, air pollution, water use, and energy consumption. The extension provides additional time to refine the regulatory framework.

event_title: McDuffie County Planning Commission Recommends Project Azelea 5-1
event_description: McDuffie County Planning Commission voted 5-1 at the Thomson-McDuffie Government Center to recommend approval of Project Azelea, a billion-dollar data center proposal. The project would be located in the Thomson area. This recommendation goes to the Board of Commissioners for a final vote.

event_title: McDuffie County Holds Public Hearing on Project Azelea Data Center
event_description: McDuffie County held a public input session on Project Azelea at the Thomson-McDuffie Government Center. Residents voiced concerns about environmental effects, water consumption from Clarks Hill Lake, potential power bill increases, noise pollution, and community disruption. The county commission final vote is anticipated for late March 2026.

event_title: Lowndes Citizens Against Data Centers Presses County for Moratorium
event_description: Lowndes Citizens Against Data Centers (LCAD) pressed the Lowndes County Board of Commissioners for a data center moratorium. On March 14, an open letter to commissioners was published in the Valdosta Daily Times urging a moratorium on the proposed DC BLOX 720-acre AI data center project. Commissioners had previously addressed the project on March 9, clarifying data center prospects for the county.
source_name: Valdosta Daily Times; Lanier County News

event_title: Project Ruby Sparks Public Concern Over 600MW Power Demand Exceeding Columbus Total Usage
event_description: Project Ruby, the proposed $5.18 billion data center in Columbus, generated significant public questions and concerns after it was revealed the facility would require approximately 600 megawatts of power—more than Columbus's entire current electricity consumption of 550 megawatts. Residents raised concerns about the impact on local power infrastructure and rates.

event_title: Dycom Industries Announces Data Center Workforce Training Center in Walton County
event_description: Dycom Industries announced plans to build a workforce training center on a 49-acre site in Walton County to train 40 workers at a time in electrical systems, fiber deployment, utility work, and maintenance. The facility will serve as a central training hub for the data center industry expansion across Georgia and the Southeast.

event_title: Atlas Development Withdraws Project Bus from Temple After Opposition
event_description: Atlas Development LLC withdrew its permitting request for Project Bus, the proposed 350-acre, $11 billion data center campus on Center Point Road in Temple. Temple Mayor Michael Johnson confirmed Atlas Development 'pulled' their application. The withdrawal followed significant community opposition, with residents near Center Point placing objection signs and more than a dozen speaking against the project at commission meetings. Commission Chairman Michelle Morgan acknowledged commissioners value citizens' voices.

event_title: Columbus Residents Pack Town Hall on $5B Project Ruby Data Center
event_description: Columbus residents packed a town hall meeting on March 18 regarding the proposed $5.18 billion Project Ruby data center. The Planning Advisory Commission was expected to take up a data center overlay district as a key step before any final Columbus City Council vote. Concerns centered on the project's 600MW power demand exceeding Columbus's entire 550MW current usage, water consumption (90,000-260,000 gpd), and infrastructure impacts.
outcome: Town hall packed; overlay under consideration

event_title: Judge Dismisses Both Lawsuits Against Columbia County Data Center Projects
event_description: A judge dismissed both lawsuits filed against the Columbia County Board of Commissioners challenging the rezoning approvals for the White Oak Business Park and Pumpkin Center data center projects. The lawsuits had alleged procedural failures in the February 3, 2026 approval process. The dismissal clears a major legal hurdle for both projects, which Commission Chairman Doug Duncan has promoted as a path to eliminating residential property taxes.
project_name: White Oak Technology Park; Pumpkin Center

event_title: Irwin Forward Data Center Application Withdrawn by Applicant
event_description: The Irwin Forward data center application for a 546.35-acre facility on Ponderosa Drive and Alapaha River Road was withdrawn by the applicant (James Russell Bryant acting for The Marcus D. Fletcher Trust) on March 2, 2026, before the scheduled Irwin County Commission hearing could take a formal vote. The Planning Commission had voted to recommend approval on February 26. The county continues to develop a data center ordinance despite the withdrawal.

event_title: Irwin County Holds Public Hearing on Data Center Ordinance
event_description: Irwin County Board of Commissioners held a public hearing on a proposed data center ordinance on March 17, 2026. The ordinance development continues despite the withdrawal of the Irwin Forward data center application on March 2. The county is establishing a regulatory framework for future data center proposals.

event_title: PSC Chairman Jason Shaw Defends 10GW Data Center Power Expansion
event_description: Georgia Public Service Commission Chairman Jason Shaw publicly defended the December 2025 decision to award Georgia Power nearly 10,000 megawatts of new capacity—largely designated for data centers and enough to power approximately 9 million homes. Two newly seated Democratic commissioners had appealed to reconsider the expansion, but that effort was blocked by the Republican majority. Shaw argued the expansion is necessary to meet projected demand and that consumer protections are adequate.

event_title: Citizens for Rural Coweta Mobilize Against Project Sail; Public Hearing Set April 7
event_description: Citizens for Rural Coweta organized opposition against the proposed Project Sail data center ($17 billion, 831 acres). Community members planned to attend the March 17 Coweta County Commission meeting wearing red shirts in opposition. A public hearing on the rezoning request was scheduled for April 7, 2026. The group, which previously collected 1,750+ petition signatures, continues to be the leading opposition organization in the county.

event_title: McDuffie County Approves Project Azelea 4-1
event_description: McDuffie County Board of Commissioners voted 4-1 to approve Project Azelea, a $1 billion data center encompassing six buildings on 200 acres near a large electrical substation with a 500kV transmission line to Plant Vogtle. The project is estimated to generate $25 million annually in local tax revenue and create 125 jobs. The approval followed the Planning Commission's 5-1 recommendation on March 3 and a March 10 public hearing where residents raised concerns about water consumption from Clarks Hill Lake, power bill increases, noise, and environmental impacts.

event_title: Port Wentworth City Council Passes Data Center Zoning Amendment Despite Planning Commission Rejection
event_description: Port Wentworth City Council voted to pass a zoning amendment defining data centers and establishing rules for size, location, and number within city limits. The amendment mandates 500-foot setbacks from residential areas. The Planning Commission had unanimously rejected the proposal on December 16, 2025, but this was a non-binding recommendation. Residents raised concerns about water use, noise, traffic, and taxes. City officials stated data center corporations are actively exploring locations in Chatham and Effingham counties, though no specific contracts exist.

event_title: QTS Files DRI for 12 Million Square Foot Project Blue Hole Data Center Campus in Blakely
event_description: QTS Technology Services (Blackstone-owned) filed a Developments of Regional Impact application with the Georgia Department of Community Affairs for Project Blue Hole in Blakely, Early County. The proposed campus would total 12 million square feet on converted farmland near Early County Airport off Martha Berry Highway, making it the largest data center pitch in South Georgia. Full build-out targeted for Q4 2035. The project will use a closed-loop water cooling system with no cooling towers and no water consumption once operational. Estimated 100+ full-time jobs at $60,000+ annually. Property owner is McKnight Blakely LLC.
source_name: AJC; Data Center Dynamics; Georgia Trend; Early County News

event_title: Georgia 2026 Legislative Session Ends (Sine Die) Without Passing Data Center Bills
event_description: The Georgia General Assembly adjourned sine die in the early morning hours of April 3, 2026, ending the 2026 legislative session without passing any major data center legislation. SB 410 (repeal sales tax exemptions, passed Senate 32-21 on March 6) died without a House vote. HB 1063 (require utilities not pass DC costs to residential customers, passed House 159-5) crossed to Senate but stalled. HB 1012 (construction moratorium through March 2027) failed. SB 34 (consumer protection) died in Rules Committee. The failure preserves approximately $2.5 billion in existing data center tax incentives. Governor Kemp had vetoed a similar tax break pause in 2024.

event_title: Coweta County Approves Project Sail $17B Data Center Rezoning 3-2
event_description: Coweta County Board of Commissioners voted 3-2 to approve the rezoning of 829 acres from Rural Conservation to Industrial for Project Sail, a $17 billion data center campus proposed by Atlas Development/Prologis. The campus will include 9 buildings totaling 4.3 million square feet. Commissioners Al Smith, Tim Castlin, and Rodney Brooks voted in favor; Bob Blackburn and John Lahman voted against. The vote followed months of intense community opposition led by Citizens for Rural Coweta, which collected 7,820 petition signatures against the project. The approval makes this the largest data center project approved in Georgia by investment value.
source_name: AJC; Newnan Times-Herald; Fox 5 Atlanta; Atlanta News First

event_title: Savannah Indivisible Hosts Data Center Town Hall at Otis Johnson Center
event_description: Savannah Indivisible hosted a data center town hall at the Otis S. Johnson Cultural Arts Center in Savannah on April 8, 2026. Chatham County Commissioner Aaron 'Adot' Whitely participated along with PSC Commissioner Peter Hubbard and PSC candidates Craig Cupid, Sheila Edwards, and Angelia Pressley. The event focused on data center growth concerns in the Savannah region, energy costs, and community impacts. The town hall drew significant community attendance and media coverage from Savannah-area outlets.
source_name: WTOC; WSAV; Savannah Tribune; Savannah Business Journal

event_title: Environmental Groups File Lawsuit Challenging Georgia PSC Data Center Power Expansion
event_description: The Southern Environmental Law Center (SELC), Sierra Club, Georgia Interfaith Power & Light, and local churches filed a 42-page lawsuit in Fulton County Superior Court challenging the Georgia Public Service Commission's December 2025 approval of nearly 10,000 megawatts of new power generation capacity, largely designated for data centers. The lawsuit alleges the expansion could cost Georgia ratepayers $50-60 billion and challenges 757 MW of allegedly unneeded capacity. The suit targets the PSC's approval of Georgia Power's Integrated Resource Plan which would add enough capacity to power approximately 9 million homes.
source_name: SELC; Claxton Enterprise; AJC; WSB-TV Atlanta

event_title: Irwin County Commission Votes on Data Center Ordinance
event_description: Irwin County Board of Commissioners voted on a proposed data center ordinance on April 6, 2026, following public hearings on March 17 and March 30, 2026. The ordinance includes provisions for closed-loop cooling system requirements and other regulatory standards for data center operations. The ordinance development was spurred by the Irwin Forward data center proposal (withdrawn March 2, 2026) and ongoing community concerns about data center impacts on rural agricultural land and groundwater resources. WWALS Watershed Coalition provided suggested additional sections for the ordinance.

event_title: DeSmog Investigative Report Highlights Rural Georgia Data Center Impacts
event_description: DeSmog published an in-depth investigative article on April 7, 2026 examining how data center development is transforming rural Georgia communities. The article details impacts on agricultural land, water resources, energy costs, and community character across multiple Georgia counties. The piece features interviews with affected residents and environmental advocates, documenting growing grassroots opposition to the data center boom in the state.

event_title: Athens-Clarke County Commission Lifts Data Center Moratorium, Adopts Ordinance
event_description: Athens-Clarke County Commission voted unanimously on April 9, 2026 to lift the temporary ban on data center development and adopt new regulations. The ordinance allows data centers in heavy industrial zones with closed-loop air conditioning system requirements to reduce water usage. Commissioners also moved forward with recommendations for water and energy consumption reporting. Commissioner Carol Myers introduced the motion; Commissioner Tiffany Taylor praised community advocacy for protection provisions. Additional refinements were subsequently sent back to the planning commission for further review.

event_title: Troup County Unveils Proposed Draft Data Center Ordinance
event_description: Troup County Board of Commissioners unveiled a proposed draft ordinance for data center zoning regulations covering unincorporated areas of the county. The ordinance excludes the cities of LaGrange, Hogansville, and West Point, which have their own zoning authority. County officials noted there are currently no active data center applications pending in Troup County. The draft comes amid ongoing countywide moratorium (extended through June 14, 2026) while the regulatory framework is developed. Project West, a proposed $9.7 billion campus, remains pending during the moratorium.

event_title: Decatur County Commissioners Approve Moratorium on Data Center Development
event_description: Decatur County Board of Commissioners voted to approve a moratorium on data center development. Commissioner Steve Brock stated 'If we don't address this now, it's going to be a problem later.' The moratorium joins neighboring South Georgia counties pressing pause on data center approvals while the county develops regulations. The vote took place at the April 14 commission meeting and also addressed a moratorium on motocross complexes. Decatur County (seat: Bainbridge) is located in southwest Georgia near the Florida border.

event_title: Columbus City Council Votes to Delay Data Center Technology Overlay District Ordinance
event_description: Columbus (Muscogee County) City Council voted without discussion to delay the first reading of an ordinance establishing a Technology Overlay District for data center regulation. Councilor Toyia Tucker (District 4) requested a 45-day delay to study best practices from other jurisdictions. The Technology Overlay District, targeting the Upatoi area, would include strict guidelines for data centers with noise provisions limiting continuous operation at specific decibel levels. The 45-day delay pushes any final vote past the May 19 mayoral and council elections. The ordinance is connected to Project Ruby, a proposed $5.18 billion hyperscale data center project.

event_title: Columbia County Resident Appeals Data Center Lawsuit Dismissals to Georgia Court of Appeals
event_description: Columbia County resident Gregory Paul Guido filed notices of appeal with the Georgia Court of Appeals challenging Superior Court dismissals of his judicial review lawsuits against the Columbia County Board of Commissioners. The appeals target the county's February 3, 2026 approval of two data center rezonings: the White Oak Business Park and Pumpkin Center projects. Guido's original February 2026 petitions alleged procedural defects, incomplete analysis, and conflicts with the county's comprehensive plan. A judge dismissed both lawsuits in March 2026; the appeals preserve appellate rights.
project_name: White Oak Technology Park; Pumpkin Center

event_title: Glynn County Commission Defers Vote on Zoning Ordinance Containing Data Center Provisions
event_description: Glynn County Commission deferred a scheduled vote on new zoning ordinances that included a controversial section permitting data centers, buried within a 235-page document. The Islands Planning Commission and Mainland Planning Commission had voted unanimously to recommend removing the data center ordinance from the vote and instead implementing a 120-day moratorium to strengthen protections. The proposed setback was 50 feet from residential zones; planners recommended 200-500 feet instead. Community opposition cited vague language and weak environmental safeguards regarding energy and water consumption. Glynn County is located on Georgia's coast (Brunswick/St. Simons area).
source_name: The Current GA; The Brunswick News

event_title: Stephens County Commission Unanimously Approves 3-Month Data Center Moratorium
event_description: Stephens County Board of Commissioners unanimously approved a three-month moratorium barring acceptance of land use applications for data centers. County Administrator Christian Hamilton cited the rationale for acting proactively while the county develops regulatory standards. Stephens County (county seat: Toccoa, northeast Georgia) has received no data center applications to date; the moratorium is a proactive measure. The decision aligns Stephens County with a growing list of Georgia counties pressing pause on data center development.

event_title: Project Arrowhead: Premier Data Center Development Proposes $6B 1.25GW Campus in Irwin County
event_description: Premier Data Center Development, LLC proposed Project Arrowhead, a five-building data center campus totaling 4.22 million sq ft on approximately 1,000 acres outside Mystic in Irwin County. The campus could total 1.25 GW of capacity with up to $6 billion in investment. Georgia Power is conducting an energy study for the project. Phase 1 could go live in 2030 with full build-out by 2034. Properties are owned by Fletcher Marcus D Trust and Sirrom Farms LLC—partially the same land previously earmarked for the withdrawn Irwin Forward Tech Park. A Change.org petition against data centers in Irwin County has over 580 signatures; the petition claims Google is the end user, though this has not been confirmed.
source_name: Data Center Dynamics; WWALS Watershed Coalition

event_title: Google Confirmed as End User for Project Pegasus; Announces $8B Expansion Plans and $1M Community Investment
event_description: Google publicly confirmed it is the end user for Project Pegasus, the $8 billion, 270-acre data center campus at 411 Pegasus Parkway in LaGrange. Google will cover 100% of power and infrastructure costs and committed a $1 million donation to Groundswell SOUL (Save On Utilities Long-term) for senior and family utility efficiency upgrades. Existing Building A is targeting 2026 operation with Buildings B and C scheduled for 2029. The site was originally acquired by Thor Equities/Form8tion in 2024; Google's identity had not been publicly confirmed until this announcement. This is Google's second Georgia data center (first is in Lithia Springs, Douglas County).

event_title: Joint Development Authority Unanimously Approves $3M Meta PILOT Dispersal Across Newton, Walton, Morgan, Jasper Counties
event_description: The Joint Development Authority of Jasper, Morgan, Newton, and Walton counties voted unanimously on April 23, 2026 to disperse $3 million in Meta PILOT (Payment In Lieu Of Taxes) payments from Meta's Stanton Springs data center campus. The split: Newton County $1.125M (37.5%), Walton County $1.125M (37.5%), Morgan County $450K (15%), Jasper County $300K (10%). Meta is scheduled to pay $8 million total to the JDA in 2026 from its two completed data center projects, with additional dispersals to follow. Payment is ahead of schedule.
source_name: Rockdale Newton Citizen; The Covington News

event_title: Sen. Ossoff Opens FERC Inquiry on AI Data Center Impact on Georgia Power Bills
event_description: U.S. Sen. Jon Ossoff (D-GA) launched a formal inquiry asking FERC Chair Laura Swett to evaluate whether AI data center expansion is driving up electricity costs for Georgia ratepayers and whether voluntary tech-company 'Ratepayer Protection Pledges' are enforceable. The April 20 letter posed four questions on FERC's role in load forecasting, energy affordability, and rulemaking; FERC was asked to respond by June 1, 2026. Statewide news cycle on the inquiry hit April 24.

event_title: Project Arrowhead DRI #4689 Formally Noticed by Georgia DCA; Public Comment Through May 11
event_description: Georgia Department of Community Affairs formally noticed DRI #4689 for Project Arrowhead — Premier Data Center Development LLC's proposed five-building, 4.22M sq ft, 1.25 GW campus on approximately 1,066 acres near Mystic in Irwin County. Notice opened a two-week public comment window through May 11, 2026 via the Southern Georgia Regional Commission. Properties owned by Fletcher Marcus D Trust and Sirrom Farms LLC; build-out estimated at up to $6B by 2034.
source_name: WWALS Watershed Coalition; Data Center Dynamics

event_title: GA PSC Pushes Back on Ossoff Inquiry: Data Centers Not Affecting Power Bills
event_description: Georgia PSC Chairman Jason Shaw and Commissioner Tricia Pridemore sent a formal letter to FERC Chair Laura Swett rebutting Sen. Ossoff's inquiry. The PSC stated data centers are not currently affecting Georgia residential power bills and cited the January 2025 PSC rule requiring large-load customers (100+ MW) to pay upstream generation costs. The letter characterized Ossoff's inquiry as based on a flawed premise.

event_title: PSC District 5 Primary Debates Dominated by Data Center Cost Allocation Concerns
event_description: Republican and Democratic candidates for the Georgia PSC District 5 primary debated at the Atlanta Press Club Loudermilk-Young series. Data center cost allocation, Georgia Power rates, and recent PSC expansion approvals dominated both debates. Republican candidates Bobby Mehan, Carolyn Roddy, and Josh Tolbert clashed over rate increases and large-load cost recovery; Mehan pledged 'no new rate increases.' Democratic candidates Craig Cupid, Shelia Edwards, and Angelia Pressley converged on affordability and tougher PSC oversight of Georgia Power's data-center-driven generation buildout. The May 19 primary is widely framed as determining PSC majority control.

event_title: Calhoun City Council Unanimously Adopts 90-Day Preemptive Data Center Moratorium
event_description: The four-member Calhoun City Council unanimously enacted a 90-day preemptive moratorium (running through approximately July 27, 2026) that halts all data center applications for zoning decisions, land-disturbance permits, and licenses within the city. City Attorney Brandon Bowen and staff were directed to draft new ordinance requirements during the pause. No active data center applications are on file in the city.
source_name: Northwest Georgia News (Calhoun Times); Coosa Valley News

event_title: Plant Wansley Groundbreaking: 1,453 MW Gas + 500 MW Battery Storage to Serve Data Center Load
event_description: Georgia Power, joined by U.S. Department of Energy officials and elected leaders, held a groundbreaking ceremony at the retired Plant Wansley site on the Heard/Carroll County line. The project includes two new combined-cycle natural-gas units (1,453 MW total) plus a 500 MW battery energy storage system, financed in part by a $26.5B DOE loan-guarantee package. Georgia Power cited 9,000+ MW of contracted data center load as the driver. Multi-county event — Heard primary site; Carroll County also affected.
source_name: Atlanta News First; Georgia Power; FOX 5 Atlanta

event_title: Project Ruby Site Map Released: Four-Building Data Center on Eastern 15% of 865-Acre Tract
event_description: Choose Columbus (the Development Authority of Columbus) and Habitat Real Estate Partners (via Muscogee Property 1 LLC) released a site map showing where the proposed hyperscale Project Ruby data center would be built within an 865-acre tract in northeastern Muscogee County, bordering Harris and Talbot counties. Four buildings would occupy roughly 15% of the site on the eastern side, near a high-voltage substation. Estimated capital investment $5.18B+ between 2027-2030; projected $68.7M/yr in property tax revenue at full build-out and 195 jobs at $80-120K. Columbus Council's first reading of the technology overlay ordinance set for May 12.

event_title: Tovey Withdraws Two Kingsland Data Center Rezoning Applications After Kings Bay Objection
event_description: Florida businessman Kirk Tovey withdrew two rezoning applications covering approximately 700 acres in Kingsland and unincorporated Camden County (including a 146-acre proposed annexation into Kingsland) tied to a planned data center development. Withdrawal followed environmental concerns and an unusual public objection from the commander of Naval Submarine Base Kings Bay. Two related items were pulled from the May 4 Kingsland Planning & Zoning agenda.
source_name: The Current GA; News4Jax; First Coast News

event_title: Camden Becomes First Coastal Georgia County to Adopt Data Center Moratorium
event_description: The Camden County Board of Commissioners voted to adopt a 6-month moratorium on data center development in unincorporated Camden County, becoming the first coastal Georgia county to do so. District 3 Commissioner Cody Smith authored the resolution; District 5 Commissioner Ben Casey clarified that the moratorium does not apply to incorporated cities. The adopted version excluded sections 4–7 of the proposed ordinance.

event_title: Bulloch BOC Extends Data Center and Residential Rezoning Moratoriums to December 31, 2026
event_description: Bulloch County Commissioners voted 5–0 (Commissioner Timmy Rushing absent) on a motion by Commissioner Toby Conner to extend both the data center moratorium and the residential/PUD rezoning moratorium through December 31, 2026. Conner stated Bulloch may not have the footprint for a data center.
source_name: Statesboro Herald; WTOC; The Georgia Virtue

event_title: Bulloch BOC Directs Staff to Draft Ordinance Prohibiting Data Centers in Unincorporated County
event_description: In a separate 5–0 motion the same evening, the Bulloch County Board of Commissioners directed staff to draft a zoning text amendment that would prohibit data centers entirely in unincorporated Bulloch County. The directive moves the county toward an outright ban once the ordinance is drafted and presented for a future vote.
source_name: Statesboro Herald; WTOC; The Georgia Virtue

event_title: 17 Coweta Residents File Superior Court Appeal Seeking to Void Project Sail Rezoning
event_description: Seventeen Coweta County residents and landowners filed an appeal/lawsuit in Coweta County Superior Court naming Coweta County and Atlas Development LLC as defendants. The filing asks the court to declare the April 11, 2026 3–2 BOC vote rezoning approximately 832 acres for the $17B Project Sail hyperscale data center campus void, and to enjoin further construction. Allegations include procedural violations of county ordinances and the Georgia Constitution, and water/aquifer concerns inside the Middle Chattahoochee Most Significant Groundwater Recharge Area. Filing date inferred from 'Tuesday' reporting; verify against court docket.

event_title: Social Circle Council Unanimously Approves Final 123-Acre Parcel for 450+ Acre Data Center Complex
event_description: Social Circle City Council unanimously approved annexation, rezoning, special-use permit, and future land-use map amendment for a final 123-acre parcel at 1402 Roy Malcom Road. The approval completes the zoning footprint for a data center complex now exceeding 450 acres along Fairplay Drive and Roy Malcom Road, with potential for more than 2 million sq ft of data center space (two ~250,000 sq ft buildings shown). Buildings limited to one story; developer must improve Roy Malcom Road. Social Circle straddles the Walton/Newton county line.

event_title: GA PSC Holds Two-Day FCR-27 Fuel Cost Hearings; Data Center Cost Allocation Central
event_description: The Georgia PSC convened a two-day hearing (May 5–6) on Georgia Power's 27th fuel cost recovery filing (Docket 56765). While the headline residential bill would drop ~$5.78/month, total projected fuel costs are 25% above FCR-26, with 98% of incremental load growth from commercial and industrial customers including data centers. PSC staff recommended further investigation into whether Real Time Pricing credits adequately protect non-RTP customers, termination of the natural gas hedging program ($753M cumulative losses since 2006, $273M since FCR-26), and flagged $152M in excess coal-plant costs. Decision scheduled May 28.
source_name: Georgia Recorder; WABE; Daily Energy Insider

event_title: Toombs/Emanuel/Jefferson Landowners Organize Against Plant Hatch-Wadley Transmission Line
event_description: Eastern Toombs County landowners organized opposition after learning Georgia Power intends to use eminent domain for a 45-65 mile, ~500 kV transmission line from Plant Hatch through Toombs, Emanuel, and Jefferson counties to the Wadley substation, tied to grid load including data centers. Residents led by Sara Brown and Melinda Morris gathered May 5 at First Baptist Church in Lyons with eminent-domain attorney Jordan Walker; many said they had not received a complete project map. Coverage published May 13. Multi-county corridor; Emanuel and Jefferson also affected.

event_title: Ashley Park-Wansley 500kV Line Eminent Domain Disputes Tied to Data Center Load Go Statewide
event_description: AJC, 11Alive, and WSB-TV spotlighted Georgia Power's use and threatened use of eminent domain for the ~35-mile, 500 kV Ashley Park-Wansley transmission corridor through Coweta and Fayette counties to serve at least four AI data centers. Reports cite roughly 330 affected parcels and 20-30 homes expected to be demolished. Coweta homeowner Ansley Brown disputed Georgia Power's appraisal of her mother's home; Georgia Power said it offered well above 125% of fair market value and that under 1% of acquisitions use eminent domain. Land acquisition began 2026; completion expected 2028. Event date approximate (mid-May coverage surge). Corridor also crosses Fayette, Heard, and Fulton.

event_title: Project Oak Data Center Open House Draws Shouting Opposition; Commission Candidate Removed
event_description: Developers held the data-center ordinance-required open house for 'Project Oak,' a second proposed Coweta data center (one 255-acre industrial parcel rezoned 2024, one 200-acre rural-conservation parcel; ~$40M projected tax revenue; ~28,000 gal/day water), at the Madras Community Center on May 18. Attendees shouted in opposition and County Commission District 3 candidate Tim Ryan was removed by a deputy. Resident Michele Lore said neighbors are preparing a petition opposing the rezoning; a 'Stop Project Oak' campaign is active.

event_title: DeKalb BOC Again Defers Data Center Text Amendment to June 23; Moratorium Continues
event_description: At the long-scheduled May 12 public hearing, the DeKalb County Board of Commissioners again deferred the data center text amendment that would add data centers as a permitted use in industrial areas with location, design, and review standards. No vote on the substance was taken and the 500,000 sq ft 'data center campus' definition question was not resolved. The ordinance is slated for the June 23 agenda, with a committee-of-the-whole discussion set for June 2. The application moratorium remains extended to June 23.

event_title: Columbus Council Delays Project Ruby Technology Overlay First Reading Up to 45 Days
event_description: Rather than holding the scheduled first reading of the technology overlay district amendments to the Unified Development Ordinance (the framework for the proposed ~865-acre, ~$5.18B Project Ruby hyperscale data center in NE Muscogee County), Columbus Council voted to pause. A motion by Councilor Toyia Tucker to delay any first reading for up to 45 days passed unanimously on a voice vote, pushing any vote past the May 19 city election amid significant resident opposition over water, power, and undisclosed project details.
outcome: Delayed up to 45 days (unanimous voice vote)

event_title: Gordon County Extends Data Center Moratorium to August 4 to Draft Strict Ordinance
event_description: The Gordon County Board of Commissioners voted to extend its temporary data center moratorium (originally enacted February 2026) through August 4, 2026 to allow time to draft regulations; the county currently has no data-center-specific ordinance. Chair Bud Owens said the county would protect its citizens and County Administrator Jim Ledbetter said attorneys are drafting a 'very strict ordinance.' A parallel anaerobic-digestion moratorium was also extended. Exact meeting date approximate (reported May 21).

event_title: May 19 PSC Primary: Edwards Wins Dem D5; GOP D5 Heads to Runoff; Fitz Johnson Wins D3 GOP
event_description: Georgia's May 19 PSC primary, widely framed around data center cost allocation, produced: District 5 Democrat Shelia Edwards winning outright over Angelia Pressley and Craig Cupid; the District 5 GOP race heading to a June 16 runoff between Josh Tolbert (~41%) and Bobby Mehan (~31%); and in District 3, former Commissioner Fitz Johnson narrowly winning the GOP nod over Brandon Martin (~2,948-vote margin) to face unopposed Democratic incumbent Peter Hubbard in November. If Democrats win both contested seats in November, the PSC would flip to a 3-2 Democratic majority, directly affecting data center cost-allocation policy.
outcome: Edwards wins D5 Dem; D5 GOP runoff June 16; Fitz Johnson wins D3 GOP

event_title: Georgia PSC Approves FCR-27 Stipulation 5-0; Opens New Investigation Into Data Center Fuel-Cost Allocation
event_description: The Georgia Public Service Commission voted 5-0 to approve the stipulated agreement between Georgia Power and PSC Public Interest Advocacy Staff on fuel cost recovery and storm damage recovery (~$285M/yr aggregate customer savings, ~$4.04/mo residential reduction effective June 1). Commissioner Hubbard's two amendments — to investigate fuel transportation/hedging/coal costs and to withhold 10% of disputed coal-dispatch costs — were voted down 3-2 along party lines (Hubbard and Johnson supporting; Shaw, McDonald, Pridemore opposing). Crucially, the Commission separately agreed to OPEN a new investigation into how fuel costs are allocated between large industrial customers (data centers) and residential/small-business ratepayers, after staff testimony found large industrial customers drive average fuel costs 5-11% higher per month — the cost-allocation venue Sen. Ossoff and consumer advocates had pushed for.
outcome: Stipulation approved 5-0; Hubbard amendments rejected 3-2; new fuel-cost allocation proceeding opened

event_title: Georgia Chamber Launches Data Center-Ready Community Designation and Digital Infrastructure Alliance
event_description: At its 2026 State of Energy event in Atlanta, the Georgia Chamber announced two new statewide initiatives: the Georgia Digital Infrastructure Alliance, and a Data Center-Ready Community Designation (launches summer 2026) that helps communities assess fiber, water, workforce, land use, and zoning to attract data centers. Featured speakers included Georgia Power CEO Kim Greene, Oglethorpe Power CEO Annalisa Bloodworth, MEAG CEO Jim Fuller, Gas South CEO Kevin Greiner, Google's Katie Ottenweller, and Fayette County Development Authority CEO Niki Vanderslice. Industry-side counter-framing to the year's mounting county moratoriums.

event_title: Atlanta Press Club PSC D5 GOP Runoff Debate Centers on Data Center Cost Allocation
event_description: The Atlanta Press Club hosted the Georgia PSC District 5 Republican runoff debate (Bobby Mehan vs. Josh Tolbert ahead of the June 16 runoff). Substantive policy discussion focused on data center cost allocation, residential rate impacts, and grid reliability. Mehan pledged 'no new rate increases' and cited Georgia Power's commitment to $102/yr average residential savings starting 2029; both candidates discussed contingencies if data center revenue underperforms projections and expressed reservations on near-term new nuclear due to cost.
source_name: Decaturish / Atlanta Press Club (PBS) / FOX 5 Atlanta

event_title: Statewide Tally: 32 GA Counties and 22 Cities Now Have Data Center Moratoriums or Ordinances Drafted
event_description: A composite AJC report compiled by June 1 documents that 32 Georgia counties and 22 cities now have data center moratoriums, drafted ordinances, or ordinances in drafting — a roughly threefold increase since October 2025. Palmetto, Fayetteville, and Atlanta have outright bans. Coverage cites Troup County's 17-page text amendment (1,500-ft setback, Tier 4 diesel, public sewer, rooftop-solar mandates) as a template. Separately, the Georgia Tech Energy Policy & Innovation Center (researcher Yang You) released an interactive moratorium/ordinance tracking tool at the Georgia Tech Data Center Hub — a new statewide reference resource.
project_name: Statewide tally / Georgia Tech Data Center Hub tracker
outcome: Trend documented; Georgia Tech tracker public

event_title: Augusta Public Services Committee Tables Data Center Moratorium 'Until Further Notice'
event_description: The Augusta Commission's Public Services Committee, chaired by Catherine Smith Rice, voted to table the proposed data center moratorium 'until further notice.' Commissioner Jordan Johnson pushed to bring it to the full Commission the following week, setting up the June 2 floor vote. The committee action followed a week of WRDW coverage and growing community pressure tied to the QTS Augusta campus near Fort Gordon.
outcome: Tabled at committee; full Commission expected to act June 2

event_title: Augusta Commission Unanimously Approves 49-Day Data Center Moratorium With QTS Carve-Out
event_description: The Augusta Commission unanimously approved a 49-day temporary moratorium on NEW data-center applications, giving planners time to write zoning rules. The moratorium explicitly does NOT apply to the $2B QTS Augusta project (6-building campus near Fort Gordon), which proceeds. The vote followed the May 27 committee tabling, a May 28 Augusta Metro Chamber luncheon (featuring QTS, Data Center Coalition, and Georgia Power Region Exec Kerry Bridges) defending the project, and weeks of community pressure from Haynes Station residents over QTS water use.
project_name: Augusta DC moratorium / QTS Augusta carve-out
outcome: Approved unanimously; 49-day pause on new applications; QTS exempted
source_name: WRDW / WJBF / The Augusta Press / GPB

event_title: Statesboro City Council Adopts Restrictive Data Center Ordinance 2026-01 on 3-1 Second Reading
event_description: Statesboro City Council adopted Ordinance 2026-01 on second reading 3-1 (Hendly, Johnson, Riggs in favor; Barr opposed) after residents spoke against. The revised version DROPPED the hyperscale (200-acre) category, caps data centers at 50 acres in O&B/HOC/LI/MU zones via Special Use Permit, requires closed-loop cooling on city water/sewer, and sets a ~50 dB ambient noise limit. Notable city-level allow-with-restrictions counterpoint to Bulloch County BOC's parallel direction to draft an unincorporated-county outright ban.

event_title: Lowndes County Commission Hears Citizen Opposition to DC BLOX Coleman Road Project
event_description: At the Lowndes County Commission regular session, citizens Jimmy LeFiles and George Fisher addressed the commission speaking against data centers, citing chemical safety and Withlacoochee River / Floridan Aquifer recharge concerns tied to the DC BLOX project on the Pope Langdale tract near the Foxborough subdivision (Coleman Road NW). No commission vote on data centers was held; agenda business was Coleman Road paving and the Animal Shelter build. Continues the local-opposition pattern documented since the July 2025 rezoning approval.
project_name: DC BLOX Valdosta (Coleman Road / Pope Langdale tract)
outcome: Ongoing public comment; no DC vote at session

event_title: Columbus Council Overlay Committee Holds Public Q&A on Project Ruby Data Center
event_description: The Council-appointed 'Unofficial Data Center Overlay Committee' held a public Q&A session addressing residents' concerns about Project Ruby — including water use (330,000 gpd cap vs. Chattahoochee River draw), C-weighted decibel noise mitigation, and PSC-mandated cost allocation for large-load customers. The committee is working in parallel with the delayed first reading of the Technology Overlay District ordinance for hyperscale data centers.
project_name: Project Ruby (Habitat Real Estate Partners / Muscogee Property 1 LLC)
outcome: Public Q&A held; overlay committee continues working

event_title: Greater Columbus Chamber Releases Project Ruby Review; Mayoral Candidates Weigh In
event_description: Greater Columbus Chamber of Commerce CEO Jansen Tidmore released an unofficial Chamber report prioritizing guardrails for the Technology Overlay District, and WTVM separately surveyed mayoral candidates Isaiah Hugley and Joanne Cogle on their Project Ruby stances. Adds business-community and electoral pressure layers to the in-progress overlay-ordinance debate.
outcome: Chamber report released; candidate positions surfaced

event_title: Maysville Holds Contentious Information Session on Northern Data Group Data Center
event_description: The City of Maysville (Jackson/Banks county line) held an informational session about the Northern Data Group data center project (57-acre / 120 MW HPC). Videos posted by citizen Carissa Dawn Martin documented contentious back-and-forth between residents and city officials. Marks the first verified active community opposition to a project the prior record shows was approved in mid-2025 with no opposition noted.
project_name: Northern Data Maysville (120 MW HPC, 57 acres)

event_title: Maysville Cancels Rescheduled Special Q&A Meeting on Northern Data Center; Citizens Show Up Anyway
event_description: The City of Maysville canceled the June 1 rescheduled special 'Q&A' meeting at the Maysville Fire Department, citing prior presentations on May 18 and 28 and most city representatives' unavailability. Citizens still showed up. Continues the community-opposition pattern that emerged this cycle for a project the existing dataset records as approved in 2025.

event_title: Southern Georgia Regional Commission Review of Project Arrowhead DRI #4689 Made Public
event_description: The Southern Georgia Regional Commission's final DRI review (dated May 14) for Project Arrowhead (Premier Data Center Development LLC, 1.25 GW, 1,066 acres near Mystic/Irwinville) was published and widely re-circulated by WWALS Watershed Coalition (Suwannee Riverkeeper). The review notes only two state agencies (SSRWPC and SGRC) submitted comments, that the application does not fit current Irwin County zoning, and that 15 of 15 public commenters opposed. Reinforces the organized opposition documented since the April DRI filing.
outcome: SGRC review made public; criticisms reinforce community opposition

event_title: Josh Tolbert Wins PSC District 5 GOP Runoff 59-40 Over Bobby Mehan
event_description: Josh Tolbert defeated Bobby Mehan in the June 16 Republican primary runoff for Georgia PSC District 5, ~349,208 to 235,588 (roughly 59% to 40%), advancing to the November general against Democrat Shelia Edwards and Libertarian Thomas Blooming. Tolbert had campaigned on the technical critique that the PSC 'must carefully evaluate forecasts, infrastructure plans, and cost allocation to ensure that residential customers and small businesses are not unfairly subsidizing large industrial loads' — i.e., data centers. The runoff itself reflected voter focus on data-center-driven Georgia Power rate hikes per Georgia Recorder reporting.
outcome: Tolbert wins 59-40; advances to November general

event_title: Newnan-Coweta Chamber 'Talk of the Town' Luncheon Defends Project Sail and Data Center Industry
event_description: The Newnan-Coweta Chamber of Commerce hosted a 'Talk of the Town' luncheon at Newnan Country Club featuring J.C. Witt (Prologis / Project Sail), Michael Olajubutu (Georgia Power), and Santiago Escobar (Headwaters), moderated by Georgia Power's John Pritchett. Speakers defended Project Sail and the broader data center industry's water and power footprint, framing the industry's case at the local level as the Project Sail lawsuit (filed May 5) progresses and Project Oak rezoning advances toward a July 21 hearing.

event_title: Coweta BOC Work Session Shelves Data Center Authority Idea and Tees Up Second Moratorium
event_description: At a Coweta County BOC work session, Commissioner Al Smith pitched creating a 'data center authority' to provide stricter oversight. Commissioners Reidelbach and Fisher were skeptical, and County Attorney Nathan Lee said the authority idea was unenforceable and unclear under Georgia law. The board agreed to move a second data center moratorium to the June 16 voting meeting agenda. Outcome: the authority idea was effectively shelved as drafted; the second moratorium was teed up for adoption.
project_name: Coweta Data Center Authority (concept) / second moratorium
outcome: Authority idea paused; moratorium moved to June 16 vote

event_title: Coweta BOC Unanimously Adopts Second 180-Day Data Center Moratorium Vesting Five Existing Projects
event_description: The Coweta County BOC unanimously approved a 180-day data center moratorium (expires Dec 23, 2026) halting all new permits, rezonings, land-use amendments, variances, and public hearings related to data centers. The five already-proposed Coweta DCs — including Project Sail and Project Oak — retain vested rights and are exempt. Commissioner Fisher wanted explicit limits and onsite power language built in, but the moratorium was adopted as written by County Attorney Nathan Lee per Commissioners Smith and McKenzie.
project_name: Coweta Second Data Center Moratorium (180 days)
outcome: Adopted unanimously; expires Dec 23, 2026; vests existing 5 proposed DCs
