event_title: DeKalb BOC Extends Data Center Moratorium 100 Days Through September 30 (5-2)
event_description: The DeKalb County BOC voted 5-2 to extend its data center moratorium 100 days through Sept 30, 2026, rather than let it expire June 23 with the still-deferred text amendment unresolved. Separately, AJC reported some DeKalb leaders pushing to DOUBLE the required distance between data centers and homes, parks, and trails as the staff-led text amendment is redrafted. The extension keeps the county-wide moratorium in place during the rewrite.
project_name: DeKalb DC text amendment / county-wide moratorium
outcome: Extension approved 5-2; moratorium now runs through Sept 30, 2026
source_name: Atlanta News First / FOX 5 Atlanta / AJC

event_title: Floyd County Commission Unanimously Adopts 80-Day Data Center Moratorium
event_description: The Floyd County Commission unanimously approved an 80-day moratorium on permits for new or expanded data centers, with a draft ordinance proposing 600-foot setbacks from homes, 300-foot property-line buffers, utility-capacity studies, decibel limits, and required public hearings. Final permanent ordinance targeted for August. Commissioners Scotty Hancock and Allison Watters spoke for the action. Sits alongside existing Atlas Gracie, Atlas Sassy, and Microsoft Project Firecracker activity in the county.
project_name: Floyd County DC Moratorium / draft ordinance
outcome: Adopted unanimously; final ordinance targeted for August
source_name: Northwest Georgia News / Coosa Valley News / WLAQ

event_title: 600-800 Residents Pack Marietta City Hall to Oppose Bells Ferry 108 MW Data Center
event_description: Between 600 and 800 residents overflowed Marietta City Hall chanting 'Not for us!' and 'We say no' against the already-approved 108 MW Bells Ferry Road hyperscale data center (MMM Acquisitions; rezoning granted in June 2025). More than a dozen residents spoke during public comment despite no formal data center item on the agenda; Mayor Pro Tem Andre Sims and Councilman Carlyle Kent responded publicly. Residents demanded a Marietta moratorium.
project_name: Bells Ferry Road Data Center (MMM Acquisitions, 108 MW)
outcome: Ongoing community opposition; no council action taken at meeting

event_title: Garden City Adopts Unanimous 6-Month Data Center Moratorium
event_description: Garden City Mayor Bruce Campbell and four council members unanimously approved a 6-month moratorium on accepting, processing, reviewing, or issuing any zoning permits, building permits, business licenses, conditional use permits, or variances for data center establishment, construction, or expansion in any zoning district. The action cites the absence of a defined data-center use in the existing zoning ordinance and pressure from neighboring Chatham-area moves (Kingsland April application, Port Wentworth Dec 2025 zoning, Rincon March 2026 ordinance, Camden County April 2026 moratorium). Coastal advocacy group One Hundred Miles (Jeff Beauvais) cited.

event_title: Columbus Council Adopts Technology Overlay District 6-2 — Project Ruby Regulatory Gateway
event_description: Columbus Council voted 6-2 to amend the Unified Development Ordinance creating a Technology Overlay District. Councilors Joanne Cogle (D7) and Simi Barnes (D1) voted NO; Councilors Bruce Huff (D3) and Toyia Tucker (D4) were absent. The overlay sets prerequisites — 55-75 dB noise limits, on-site water pre-treatment, Tier IV diesel generators — that any future hyperscale data center, including the $5.18B Project Ruby, must meet. Residents submitted letters in opposition. Council members noted no immediate direct effect on Project Ruby; the developer (Habitat Real Estate Partners / Muscogee Property 1 LLC) has not yet submitted the rezoning application.
project_name: Columbus Technology Overlay District (Project Ruby gateway)
outcome: Adopted 6-2 (Cogle, Barnes dissenting; Huff, Tucker absent)

event_title: Hall County Closes Public-Comment Period on Data Center Ordinance With ~106 Comments
event_description: Hall County closed its public-comment period on the in-progress data center ordinance, having collected approximately 106 public comments through community meetings (incl. a South Hall meeting drawing 38 attendees) and a North Hall session held in the lead-up to the deadline. Planning Director Katie Ahmed is leading the redraft; output feeds into the next iteration of the ordinance text. County-wide moratorium adopted Feb 26, 2026 (4-0) remains in effect.

event_title: Georgia Power Opens CARES Customer-Identified Resource Enrollment for C&I / Data Center Renewables
event_description: Georgia Power opened enrollment for the new CARES CIR (Clean And Renewable Energy Subscription - Customer Identified Resource) program approved in the 2025 IRP stipulation. The program lets commercial/industrial customers — explicitly including data centers — identify preferred renewable projects for procurement. The DG-specific RFP window remains slated for Q4 2026. Utility touts as flexibility for large-load customers; advocates note it does not address PSC-driven cost allocation concerns.
outcome: Enrollment window opened; DG RFP still slated for Q4 2026
source_name: Daily Energy Insider / Georgia Power press

event_title: QTS Augusta Community Panel at Belair Elementary Draws Skeptical Response
event_description: QTS and local officials held an hour-long community panel at Belair Elementary on the proposed Gordon Highway campus, taking pre-submitted questions from residents. Community leader Dorothy Smith (50501 Augusta) said the session 'doesn't instill a lot of confidence to hear the canned responses to the prescreened questions' and characterized responses as 'doublespeak.' QTS reiterated project stats — 170+ acres, up to 6 buildings, ~$2B, ~1,000 construction jobs, 160-220 permanent jobs, one Olympic-pool of water at startup, none for cooling after — but did not shift community sentiment.

event_title: Augusta Unveils Draft Data Center Ordinance Restricting DCs to Heavy Industrial With Special Exception
event_description: Augusta Planning & Development unveiled its Draft Data Center Ordinance for public review, scheduling three public meetings (July 6 at 3pm Planning Commission, July 14 at 1pm Public Services Committee, July 21 at 2pm Augusta Commission). The draft would restrict data centers to heavy industrial districts and require Special Exception approval (not permitted by right in any district) — materially more restrictive than the current framework and setting up a July 21 vote just as the 49-day moratorium expires.
outcome: Draft released for public review; three meetings scheduled

event_title: Augusta Planning Commission Delays Action on DC Ordinance, Asks for 60-Day Moratorium Extension
event_description: At the first public hearing on Augusta's draft data center ordinance, the Planning Commission delayed action, sent the draft forward to the Public Services Committee with NO recommendation, and asked the Augusta Commission to extend the 49-day moratorium (set to expire July 21) by 60 days — calling the draft 'rushed.' City Administrator Tameka Allen said the city would consider planning commission input before taking a recommendation to the governing body.
outcome: Sent forward with no recommendation; 60-day moratorium extension requested

event_title: DeKalb BOC Unanimously (7-0) Rejects Proposed Data Center Text Amendment as Too Weak
event_description: The DeKalb County BOC voted 7-0 to REJECT the proposed Data Center Text Amendment — which would have set a 1M sq ft campus cap and 750-ft residential buffers — after initially voting to defer to Aug 11 and then reconsidering the same evening. Residents and activists said the ordinance was too weak; the rejection forces a redraft with stricter provisions. County-wide moratorium remains in effect through Sept 30 per the June 9 extension.
source_name: Decaturish / Capital B Atlanta / WABE / Atlanta News First

event_title: Milton City Council Unanimously Enacts 30-Day Data Center Moratorium (Retro)
event_description: The Milton City Council unanimously enacted a 30-day moratorium on all data center-related applications — rezonings, LDPs, building permits, SUPs, business licenses, COs — with option to extend. City Attorney Ken Jarrard drafted. North Fulton municipality joins the growing metro Atlanta moratorium list. Note: this event dates to June 17 (inside cycle 5's Jun 6-18 window) but was missed in that cycle's search; captured here retrospectively.
outcome: Adopted unanimously; 30-day duration with option to extend

event_title: Bartow Planning Commission Recommends 5-0 New Data Center Text Amendment Tightening Rules
event_description: The Bartow County Planning Commission voted 5-0 to recommend approval of a text amendment tightening data center rules: allowed by-right in I-1/I-2/BPD zones and by CUP in A-1, with 75-ft maximum height, 50-ft setbacks, 150-ft frontage/width, 50-acre minimum lot, 200-ft buffer, required closed-loop cooling, noise limits (65 dBA day / 55 dBA night, +3/+0 dBA ambient), and a $1,000/day fine for violations. Community Development Director Brandon Johnson led the presentation. Sole Commissioner Steve Taylor scheduled to take up the recommendation at his July 1 public meeting.
outcome: Recommended approval 5-0; Sole Commissioner takeup July 1

event_title: DataBank Files DRI for 200 MW 'Project Indo' Data Center Campus in Cartersville
event_description: DataBank filed a Development of Regional Impact application with the Georgia Department of Community Affairs for 'Project Indo' — a 200 MW, 1.1M sq ft data center campus on 69 acres at 218 Industrial Park Rd, Cartersville, seeking a 288 MW grid connection. Estimated ~$2.4B project. Filed the same day the Planning Commission recommended tighter DC rules — creating a live tension between Bartow's regulatory tightening and continued industry interest.
project_name: Project Indo (DataBank, 200 MW / 1.1M sq ft / 69 ac / $2.4B)

event_title: SELC and Coalition Alert GA EPD to Unpermitted Construction at VoltaGrid/Serverfarm Covington 'Pop-Up' Power Plant
event_description: Sustainable Newton, Altamaha Riverkeeper, and the Southern Environmental Law Center sent a formal letter to GA EPD Branch Chief James Boylan demanding investigation and enforcement against VoltaGrid (33 planned natural-gas Jenbacher J620 engines; 7-8 already built as of June 19) and Serverfarm (36 of 37 diesel emergency gensets installed) at the Covington 'pop-up' power-plant + data-center site — alleging construction began before Georgia SIP-required preconstruction air permits were issued. AJC ran a same-day feature framing it as 'Georgia's first data-center pop-up power plant' and elevating the story statewide.
project_name: VoltaGrid Covington 90 MW / Serverfarm Covington DC
outcome: Enforcement letter filed; GA EPD asked for stop-work and penalties
source_name: SELC / AJC / Atlanta News First / Rockdale-Newton Citizen

event_title: Douglas County Data Center Watchdogs First Informational Meeting Draws 100+ Attendees
event_description: The first informational meeting of the Douglas County Data Center Watchdogs drew 100+ attendees to a local library, focusing on land-use rights, water demand, and tax incentives ahead of the July 7 public hearing on East Village Dothan LLC's proposed 700+ acre, 11-building, 6.2M sq ft campus south of I-20 near Liberty Road (Villa Rica boundary). Organized community opposition emerging in a county otherwise home to Google, Microsoft, AWS, and DC BLOX campuses.
project_name: East Village Dothan LLC (700+ ac, 11 buildings, 6.2M sq ft)
outcome: Organizing meeting; July 7 public hearing scheduled

event_title: Marietta P&Z Revisits Powers Ferry Place 18 MW Data Center Rezoning; Residents Oppose
event_description: The Marietta P&Z Commission revisited a rezoning proposal for a 10.7-acre CRC-zoned property at 1155 Powers Ferry Place (adjacent to I-75 and ReNew Cobb apartments) to convert an existing storage facility into an 18 MW data center. Residents voiced opposition. Commission's recommendation will go to the Marietta City Council on July 8 (outside window). Second Marietta DC pressure point after the June 10 Bells Ferry 108 MW protest.
project_name: 1155 Powers Ferry Place Data Center (18 MW, 10.7 ac)
outcome: Hearing held; recommendation to City Council July 8

event_title: Keep It Rural Files Superior Court Lawsuit Against Columbus Technology Overlay and Project Ruby
event_description: Keep It Rural LLC and eight Upatoi-area landowners filed a seven-count complaint in Muscogee County Superior Court against the Columbus Consolidated Government and Mayor Skip Henderson, seeking a TRO and asking the court to VOID the June 16 Technology Overlay ordinance that enables the $5.18B Project Ruby data center. The ordinance was scheduled to take effect June 28. The lawsuit is Columbus's first major legal challenge to the Project Ruby framework.
outcome: Complaint filed; TRO sought; ordinance takes effect June 28 pending court action

event_title: Franklin County BOC Work Session Reaches Consensus to Pursue 6-Month to 1-Year Data Center Moratorium
event_description: At the June 30 Franklin County BOC work session, the Board reached consensus to pursue a 6-month to 1-year data center moratorium. Commissioner Busby's draft ban was discussed; County Attorney Patel suggested a temporary moratorium approach; Commissioner Smith stated outright opposition to data centers on farmland. Two residents spoke — Cheryl Riddle (Commerce) and Bruce Scranton (Franklin Springs). First documented DC discussion in a county with No Activity on record.
outcome: Consensus to pursue moratorium; formal vote to follow

event_title: Georgia PSC Unanimously Opens Data Center Fuel-Cost Allocation Investigation; September Hearings Set
event_description: The PSC voted unanimously July 7 to open the investigation Georgia Power agreed to in the May 28 FCR-27 settlement, targeting Real-Time Pricing / large-load cost shifting — staff testimony projects up to 11%/month residential impact by 2028. First evidentiary hearings set for September; investigation to conclude by end of 2026. Commissioner Hubbard's push for a broader 'holistic' scope was voted down by the GOP majority. Boundary event (July 7) resolved after prior cycle's cutoff.
outcome: Investigation opened unanimously; Sept hearings; concludes by end of 2026

event_title: SELC Petitions PSC Alleging VoltaGrid's 90 MW Covington Power Sale Violates Georgia Territorial Act
event_description: SELC, on behalf of Sustainable Newton, filed a PSC complaint arguing VoltaGrid's planned 90 MW power sale to separately-owned Serverfarm violates the Georgia Territorial Electric Service Act and the Cogeneration & Distributed Generation Act, asking the PSC to halt unlawful operations. Follows Commissioner Hubbard's request that staff explore a Territorial Act investigation.

event_title: Georgia Chamber Formally Launches Digital Infrastructure Alliance and Data Center Ready Community Designation
event_description: The Georgia Chamber formally launched the Georgia Digital Infrastructure Alliance and the Data Center Ready Community Designation (fiber, water, workforce, zoning readiness assessments), announced in May at the State of Energy event. CEO Chris Clark framed it as preparing communities for 'responsible' data center investment. Industry-side counterweight to the accelerating county moratorium wave.

event_title: Gov. Kemp Joins Trump 'Ratepayer Protection Pledge' on Data Center Infrastructure Costs
event_description: Gov. Brian Kemp appeared at a White House roundtable as one of 23 GOP governors joining the Trump administration's voluntary pledge requiring data center builders/users to pay for the infrastructure and generation serving them. Kemp said the pledge supports nuclear plants while keeping local rates low — aligning the governor with the ratepayer-protection framing that has dominated the PSC races.
outcome: Kemp signs pledge with 22 other GOP governors

event_title: 'Connected Georgia' Industry PR Campaign Revealed as Legislature Weighs Data Center Regulation
event_description: Georgia Recorder revealed 'Connected Georgia,' an arm of the Data Center Coalition-linked America Connects, launched a statewide image campaign (website June 15; YouTube ad with 2M+ views) amid the statewide backlash and after all 2026 data-center bills died. Sierra Club GA lobbyist Mark Woodall: 'trying to put lipstick on a pig.' Signals the industry pivot from lobbying to public persuasion ahead of the 2027 session.
outcome: Campaign revealed; legislative regulation debate continues

event_title: GA EPD Issues Stop-Work Order and NOVs to VoltaGrid and Serverfarm Over Unpermitted Covington Construction
event_description: GA EPD publicly revealed it issued Notices of Violation (dated July 2, after a June 25 tip and June 29 site visit) to VoltaGrid and Serverfarm for building gas engines and generators without air permits, ordered VoltaGrid to immediately halt all construction, and demanded explanations with monetary penalties possible. Serverfarm has since received its air permit. Resolves the SELC coalition enforcement letter (logged July 2) with the strongest state enforcement action of the DC buildout to date.
outcome: Stop-work ordered; NOVs issued; penalties pending

event_title: Douglas County BOC Denies East Village Dothan 700-Acre Data Center Campus 4-1
event_description: The Douglas County BOC voted 4-1 to deny East Village Dothan LLC's (EdgeConneX-linked) 700-acre, ~4.4-6.2M sq ft campus south of I-20 at Liberty Road — the second denial for this site in seven months. Opponents packed the hearing with noise-audio props following the Data Center Watchdogs organizing (100+ at June 23 meeting). Boundary event (July 7) resolved after prior cycle's cutoff.
project_name: East Village Dothan LLC (700 ac / 11 bldgs / 6.2M sq ft)
outcome: Denied 4-1; second denial in seven months
source_name: Douglas County Sentinel / FOX 5 Atlanta / DCD

event_title: DeKalb BOC Extends Data Center Moratorium Through March 30, 2027; Terry Casts Lone No
event_description: The DeKalb BOC extended the county-wide data center moratorium through March 30, 2027 — superseding the Sept 30 horizon set June 9 — after the July 23 unanimous rejection of the text amendment forced a full redraft. Commissioner Ted Terry cast the lone no vote, blasting 'internal' CEO-led studies versus independent ones; his environmental/health study resolution was deferred to July 14. Commissioner Patrick moved to reconsider the rejected regulations.
project_name: DeKalb DC text amendment / county moratorium

event_title: Gordon County Extends Data Center Moratorium Through January 29, 2027
event_description: The Gordon County BOC extended its data center (and anaerobic digestion) moratoriums through January 29, 2027, superseding the Aug 4 expiry and the August-ordinance plan. The board canceled the July 13 P&Z public hearing and promised at least one town hall before any ordinance adoption.
outcome: Extended through Jan 29, 2027; town hall promised

event_title: Marietta Tables Powers Ferry 18 MW Data Center 7-0 and Enacts Six-Month Citywide Moratorium
event_description: At the same July 8 meeting, the Marietta City Council voted 7-0 to table the 1155 Powers Ferry Place 18 MW 'transmission-of-information facility' rezoning until August after protests filled City Hall, then unanimously enacted a six-month moratorium on new data center projects through Dec 31, 2026 (exempting the Powers Ferry application and the approved Bells Ferry DC). Developer attorney Chuck Clay represented the applicant.
project_name: Marietta DC moratorium / 1155 Powers Ferry Place (18 MW)
source_name: MDJ / Atlanta News First / WSB-TV / East Cobb News

event_title: Milton Extends Data Center Freeze 180 More Days
event_description: The Milton City Council unanimously extended its data center freeze another 180 days, following the initial 30-day moratorium enacted June 17 and a prior extension. North Fulton's pause now runs into early 2027 while the city drafts permanent regulations.

event_title: Chamblee Adopts 180-Day Data Center Moratorium Through January 16, 2027
event_description: The Chamblee City Council unanimously adopted a 180-day moratorium on data center development and applications through January 16, 2027, led by At-Large Councilmember Jimmy Furst — the first DeKalb municipality to enact its own pause on top of the county's March 2027 moratorium.
source_name: Decaturish / FOX 5 / Atlanta News First / City of Chamblee

event_title: Cherokee County BOC Unanimously Approves 30-Day Data Center Moratorium
event_description: The Cherokee County BOC unanimously approved a 30-day data center moratorium so staff can draft regulations; staff will request a 180-day extension in August (running to ~mid-February 2027). First DC action in a county with no prior data center activity on record.
outcome: Adopted unanimously; 180-day extension request expected in August
source_name: WSB-TV / Atlanta News First / Cherokee Tribune

event_title: Coweta BOC Continues Project Oak Rezoning Hearing to August 25 at Applicant's Request
event_description: The Coweta BOC public hearing on Rezone 24-020 (LDO Coweta LLC, ~464 ac, 6 buildings / 895,530 sq ft — Project Oak) was continued to August 25 at the applicant's request after a portion of the property was withdrawn from the amended application. No vote occurred. Project Oak retains vested rights under the county's 180-day moratorium.
outcome: Hearing continued to Aug 25; no vote

event_title: Paulding County BOC Unanimously Suspends Data Center Applications Until January 1, 2027
event_description: The Paulding County BOC unanimously suspended new data center applications, zoning requests, and civil plan reviews until January 1, 2027 to overhaul land-use codes — drawing applause from residents after months of protests over zoning loopholes. First DC action in a county with no prior activity on record.

event_title: Stillwater Development Files DRI for 1.25 GW / $13B Stillwater Technology Park in Lovejoy
event_description: Stillwater Development filed a DRI for Stillwater Technology Park: up to 1.25 GW, 15 buildings / 3.465M sq ft on ~400 acres in Lovejoy, ~$13B, first phase by 2031. Clayton County's moratorium does not apply inside Lovejoy city limits — a jurisdictional gap likely to become a flashpoint. Filed the same day as OpenAI's Effingham DRI and Google's Troup DRI per The Current.

event_title: Google Files DRI #4797 for $1B Expansion of LaGrange Pegasus Parkway Campus
event_description: Google filed DRI #4797 with GA DCA for a ~$1B, 470,000 sq ft additional building at its Pegasus Parkway LaGrange campus, with work through 2029 and possible future phases. Filed the same day as the OpenAI Effingham and Stillwater Lovejoy DRIs — a coordinated pipeline surge amid the moratorium wave.

event_title: Troup County Commissioners Approve Data Center Ordinance and Lift Moratorium (Retro — Date Confirmed)
event_description: Troup County commissioners approved a 17-page data center text amendment (1,500-ft residential setbacks, Tier 4 diesel generators, public sewer requirement, rooftop solar mandates — cited by AJC as a statewide template) and lifted the county's moratorium. RETRO ENTRY: this event was held out of the May 10-22 cycle pending date confirmation (LaGrange Daily News egress-blocked); the May 8, 2026 date is now confirmed via WSB Radio and subsequent AJC references.
project_name: Troup County DC ordinance (17-page text amendment)

event_title: Augusta Committee Takes No Action on Data Center Ordinance as Moratorium Deadline Looms
event_description: Augusta commissioners at the Public Services Committee took no action on the draft data center ordinance (heavy-industrial-only + Special Exception), sending it to the full commission with the 49-day moratorium expiring July 21. Members debated 30 vs. 60-day extensions without agreement. Planning Director Lisa Cameron called the draft a 'living document'; staff still recommended adoption. QTS Gordon Highway explicitly unaffected.
outcome: No committee action; sent to full commission

event_title: Augusta Commission Unanimously Extends Data Center Moratorium 60 Days Instead of Adopting Ordinance
event_description: The full Augusta Commission voted unanimously to extend the data center moratorium 60 days rather than adopt the draft ordinance, after 11 residents cited utility costs, water quality, and a rushed process. Three more public meetings scheduled (Warren Road, Diamond Lakes, Henry Brigham community centers) plus a commissioner site visit to an Atlanta-area data center Aug 3 (Mayor Pro-Tem Wayne Guilfoyle: buffers/noise focus). Final decision now points toward the Aug 18 meeting window.
outcome: Extended 60 days unanimously; ordinance not adopted

event_title: Georgia Power Holds Swainsboro Public Meeting on Hatch-Wadley 500kV Transmission Line
event_description: Georgia Power held a public information meeting at The Nordson Center in Swainsboro on the proposed 75-mile Hatch-Wadley 500kV transmission line (Plant Hatch, Appling Co. to Wadley Primary Substation, Jefferson Co., crossing Toombs and Emanuel), following survey and eminent-domain notices to landowners. First logged DC-related event for Emanuel County.
outcome: Info meeting held; easement acquisition Q4 2026

event_title: Georgia Power Vidalia Sessions Confirm 403 Parcels Affected by Hatch-Wadley Line; Landowners Organizing
event_description: Georgia Power held two info sessions in Vidalia with 50+ staff. Rep Joshua Peacock confirmed ~403 parcels affected and acknowledged data centers as a driver ('We have not been shy about the fact that data centers are coming to Georgia'). Timeline: easement acquisition Q4 2026, clearing Q1 2027, construction Q4 2027, completion Q1 2031. A local landowner group (contact Sara Brown) is actively meeting to discuss options.
outcome: Sessions held; 403 parcels confirmed; landowners organizing

event_title: Citizens Ask Toombs County Commission to Enact Land-Use Ordinances Ahead of Data Center Development
event_description: At the July 21 Toombs County Commission meeting, several citizens — including Hatch-Wadley landowner organizer Sara Brown — asked commissioners to review and enact land-use ordinances to prepare for future developments such as data centers. Proactive-restrictive posture emerging in a county with no zoning framework for DCs.
outcome: Citizen request; no commission action yet

event_title: OpenAI Announces $20B, 3.2 GW 'Project Camellia' Data Center Campus — Largest in Company History
event_description: OpenAI announced its largest-ever data center campus: $20B, 3.2 GW, ~1,400 acres at the Savannah Gateway Industrial Hub in Effingham County — one of the largest private investments in coastal Georgia history. ~400 long-term jobs; powered in part by a new combined-cycle unit at Georgia Power's Plant McIntosh (Rincon); significant tax abatements; DRI filed the same day. Deal negotiated in secret with no prior public input — energy ramp 2028-2032. Same-day DRI filings by Stillwater (Clayton) and Google (Troup) made July 22 the biggest pipeline day of the year.
outcome: Announced; DRI filed; state evaluation next
source_name: The Current / GPB / WTOC / Effingham Herald

event_title: ~300 Residents Protest Outside OpenAI Open House Over Project Camellia Secrecy
event_description: A crowd of roughly 300 gathered outside the Effingham College & Career Academy to protest Project Camellia while OpenAI held an open house inside. Anger centered on the secrecy of the deal, tax abatements, and water/energy impacts. Follow-on accountability reporting (Effingham Herald: 'How OpenAI's Effingham Data Center Moved Forward Without Public Input') amplified the transparency critique.

event_title: Franklin County BOC Formally Adopts Data Center Moratorium Through December 8, 2026 (Retro)
event_description: The Franklin County BOC voted unanimously July 6 to impose a data center moratorium, shortened on County Attorney Prya Patel's advice to run through Dec 8, 2026 (Commissioners Pulliam and Chair Long absent). Formalizes the June 30 work-session consensus already logged. RETRO ENTRY: vote occurred two days before this cycle's window; reported July 8.

event_title: Terrell County BOC Unanimously Adopts 6-Month Data Center Moratorium
event_description: The Terrell County BOC voted unanimously to pause new data centers for six months while drafting zoning regulations, though no proposal is pending. Chair W.T. Gamble III cited $20-30M/yr potential tax revenue but wants rules first. First logged DC event for Terrell County. Boundary event (July 7).

event_title: Early County Commissioners Unanimously Adopt Data Center Ordinance With Water, Noise, and Buffer Rules
event_description: Early County commissioners unanimously passed a data center ordinance (regulation, not a ban): water-efficient cooling required, noise limits, and a 1,000-ft buffer from homes, schools, and churches. Packed meeting at the Early County Theatre; residents said it doesn't go far enough. Managed-development posture in a county facing the Georgia-Pacific mill closure.

event_title: Citizens Pack Americus Council Over Data Center Ordinance; 90-Day Moratorium Requested
event_description: Heavy citizen attendance at the Americus City Council over the proposed data center ordinance (first discussed July 16); Kirk Lyman-Barner requested a 90-day moratorium to get the ordinance right. A proposed Americus data center site was confirmed in subsequent reporting (July 27). First logged DC events for Sumter County.
outcome: Citizen pressure; 90-day moratorium requested; ordinance pending

event_title: 'Stop Hyperscale Data Centers in Muscogee County' Rallies Downtown Against Project Ruby
event_description: The group 'Stop Hyperscale Data Centers in Muscogee County' rallied downtown Saturday against Project Ruby and the Technology Overlay, demanding a moratorium and citing lack of transparency. Sustained organized opposition while the Keep It Rural lawsuit proceeds.

event_title: Columbus Files ~400-Page Response in Keep It Rural Lawsuit Defending Technology Overlay
event_description: Columbus filed a ~400-page response in the Keep It Rural lawsuit, arguing the Technology Overlay 'does not rezone any property or authorize construction of a data center.' No TRO ruling or hearing had occurred as of July 31; next step is a ruling or hearing date. The Project Ruby rezoning application has still not been filed by the developer.
project_name: Keep It Rural v. Columbus / Technology Overlay
outcome: City response filed; no ruling yet

event_title: Dougherty County Commission Approves 45-Day Resolution to Review Data Center Zoning
event_description: Dougherty County commissioners approved a 45-day resolution to review zoning for data centers — the county-level counterpart to the City of Albany's parallel moratorium debate (6-18 month pause weighed July 21). First logged DC events for Dougherty County.

event_title: Albany City Commission Unanimously Adopts 12-Month Data Center Moratorium
event_description: The Albany City Commission unanimously paused data center development for 12 months to draft regulations, following the July 21 session where commissioners weighed a 6-18 month pause ('Data centers are already in Georgia').

event_title: Warner Robins Approves 6-Month Data Center Moratorium to Study Water, Sewer, and Grid Impacts
event_description: Mayor LaRhonda Patrick and the Warner Robins City Council approved a moratorium of at least six months (through ~January 2027) to study water table, sewer, and grid impacts before considering any data center. First logged DC event for Houston County. Minor date ambiguity: vote reported as 'Monday' before the July 21 story — July 20 most likely (a July 7 council discussion preceded it).

event_title: Lowndes Commission Directs Staff to Draft DC Ordinance by September; Chairman Declares 'Verbal Moratorium'
event_description: After the regular session, County Manager Paige Dukes presented a data center briefing; commissioners directed staff to draft an ordinance by ~September. Chairman Bill Slaughter: 'We are not going to move forward with a datacenter in Lowndes County until we have an ordinance in place.' LAKE criticized the unwritten moratorium's legal standing. Context: Brooks Co., Cook Co., and the City of Adel have already passed moratoriums; the Foxborough 'Backyard Battle' organizing against the DC BLOX/Langdale ~720-acre AI campus continued (WALB July 24).
project_name: Lowndes DC ordinance (directed) / DC BLOX Coleman Rd
outcome: Ordinance directed by September; verbal moratorium declared

event_title: Northern Data/Rumble Hold Maysville Town Hall on 120 MW HPC Site
event_description: Northern Data/Rumble leadership held the long-promised community town hall at the Jackson County Agriculture Facility in Jefferson, presenting building concepts, economic benefits, water/utility impacts, and sound/lighting/security plans for the ~60-acre, 120 MW site at 121 Industrial Drive. Citizen opposition remains active; Maysville's council separately directed the city attorney (July 6) to draft a moratorium resolution for future data centers (won't affect Northern Data).

event_title: Google Named Sole End-User and Operator of 8M Sq Ft Columbia County Data Center
event_description: The Columbia County Economic Development Authority announced Google as the 'sole end-user and operator' of the Columbia County Data Center — 23 buildings totaling 8M sq ft across 1,900 acres northwest of White Oak Business Park (Trammell Crow / CBRE, DRI filed April 2025). BOC Chairman Doug Duncan called it 'one of the most significant investments in our county's history' and appeared onstage in Washington with President Trump at the Ratepayer Protection Pledge expansion event (the same event Gov. Kemp attended). The project has drawn controversy since 2025 including citizen lawsuits (dismissed March, appealed April). ANALYST-FLAGGED: surfaced by Mike post-report; verified via DCD + named GA officials.
project_name: Columbia County Data Center (Google / Trammell Crow, 8M sq ft / 1,900 ac)
outcome: Google announced as end user July 23; construction pipeline proceeds
source_name: Data Center Dynamics / Columbia County EDA

event_title: Roswell Council Approves First Reading 5-0 of UDC Data Center Amendment
event_description: The Roswell Mayor and Council approved (5-0) the first reading of a Unified Development Code amendment on data centers — defining 'data centers' and setting standards for noise, water, and energy consumption. The amendment stems from months of staff research (27-page white paper) and two public hearings during the moratorium in place since Jan 12 (extended March 23; third extension sought). No formal adoption yet — the vote is expected at a future council meeting (next regular meeting Aug 10). ANALYST-FLAGGED: surfaced by Mike post-report; verified via the city's official Roswell Connections recap.
outcome: First reading approved 5-0; adoption vote at future meeting
source_name: Roswell Connections (City of Roswell) / The Georgia Sun

event_title: Project Arrowhead Public Event Held at Irwinville Community Center Amid Continued WWALS Opposition
event_description: A citizen/public meeting on the 1,066-acre, up-to-1.25 GW Project Arrowhead (DRI #4689) was held at the Irwinville Community Center. WWALS Watershed Coalition continues opposition over Alapaha River / Floridan Aquifer withdrawal. No DCA or BOC final decision has been reported.
outcome: Public event held; DCA decision still pending

event_title: PSC Reviews OpenAI-Georgia Power Contract; Hubbard Warns of 'Loopholes' Ahead of Aug 14 Auto-Effective Date
event_description: The Georgia PSC is reviewing the Georgia Power-OpenAI electric service contract for Project Camellia, filed July 15 as a 100-page unsigned agreement under the PSC's April 2025 rule requiring 30-day pre-execution filing for DC contracts over 100 MW. Commissioner Hubbard expects it to take effect August 14 with no commission vote required and warns of contract 'loopholes' — early-termination risk leaving ratepayers with stranded infrastructure and 'no provision for clean energy' ('I just don't trust that the AI bubble is not going to burst'). Commissioner Fitz Johnson counters that GA protections are 'among the strongest in the country' but 'have to be enforced.'
project_name: Project Camellia contract (Georgia Power / OpenAI, 3.2 GW / 25-yr)

event_title: Southern Co. Contracted Large Load Hits 17 GW; OpenAI Deal Includes First Codified 1 GW Flexible Demand Provision
event_description: Utility Dive reports Southern Company's contracted large load rose to 17 GW (+6 GW since Q1), driven by Georgia Power's 3.2 GW / 25-year OpenAI contract — which includes 1 GW of 'flexible demand response,' the first flexibility provision Southern has codified with a data center customer. Pipeline exceeds 75 GW with 8 GW in advanced contracting; data center usage +55% YoY. CEO Chris Womack: 'There's noise all across the country about data centers... we've got to do a better job,' emphasizing minimum bills, termination payments, and collateral protections.
project_name: Georgia Power large-load portfolio / OpenAI flexibility provision
outcome: 17 GW contracted; 1 GW DR provision codified

event_title: GA Advocates Alarmed by EPA Plan to Strip Public Notice From Minor-Source Air Permits; VoltaGrid Still Unpermitted
event_description: GPB/Ledger-Enquirer report Georgia clean-air advocates and DC opponents are alarmed by EPA's proposal to strip public notice and comment from state 'minor source' air permits — the mechanism through which GA groups learned of and delayed DC generator projects (comments close Aug 21). GA-specific data: 20 minor-source DC generator permits approved since Jan 2025 vs. 17 total in 2014-2024; Sierra Club analysis counts 2,600+ approved diesel generators (~5.2 GW) across 24 named GA data centers. Progression on Covington: Serverfarm has now received its air permit; VoltaGrid still has NOT and both 'remain liable for penalties and further enforcement actions.'
project_name: GA minor-source air permits / VoltaGrid-Serverfarm Covington
outcome: EPA comment period closes Aug 21; VoltaGrid unpermitted; penalties pending

event_title: Bottoms Pledges Statewide Data Center Pause at Georgia Chamber Luncheon; Jackson Rejects Moratorium
event_description: At the Georgia Chamber annual luncheon in Athens before 1,000+ business leaders, Democratic gubernatorial nominee Keisha Lance Bottoms said she would support a temporary statewide pause on data center construction ('I just want us to pause... we don't have enough facts') — the first explicit statewide-pause commitment from a major-party nominee. Republican Rick Jackson rejected a moratorium in favor of full local control and pitched data centers as a way to eliminate county property taxes. Data centers are now a defining issue of the governor's race.
outcome: Bottoms pause pledge; Jackson local-control counter

event_title: Stillwater Withdraws 1.25 GW / $13B Lovejoy Data Center Campus at Special Called Session
event_description: Stillwater Development formally withdrew its 15-building, ~3.5M sq ft, 1.25 GW, ~$13B data center campus at 11760 Panhandle Road at a special called Lovejoy City Council session held for the sole purpose of the withdrawal. Mayor Marci Fluellyn said the developers will pursue residential development instead. A major opposition win just 15 days after the July 22 DRI filing — the jurisdictional gap (county moratorium not applying inside Lovejoy) closed by community pressure rather than regulation.
outcome: Withdrawn Aug 6; site to be pursued as residential

event_title: West End Residents and NPUs Mobilize Against Digital Realty Exception Ahead of Aug 10 Zoning Vote
event_description: ATL Press Collective reports residents and Neighborhood Planning Units organizing ahead of the Aug 10 City Council Zoning Committee vote on Councilman Antonio Lewis's ordinance amendment carving an exception to Atlanta's MARTA/Beltline data center ban for a $500M Digital Realty project near the West End MARTA station. The committee previously tabled 6-1; NPUs S, T, and X plus the Atlanta Planning Advisory Board have formally opposed. Tests the durability of Atlanta's Sept 2024 ban.
project_name: Digital Realty West End ($500M) / MARTA-Beltline ban exception
outcome: Organizing continues; Zoning Committee vote Aug 10
source_name: ATL Press Collective / AJC / Capital B Atlanta

event_title: Bulloch BOC Tables Outright Data Center Ban 30 Days to September Agenda
event_description: The Bulloch County BOC heard the P&Z-recommended zoning text amendment removing data centers and crypto mining from county zoning entirely — which would have been Georgia's first county-level outright DC ban — but voted to TABLE it for 30 days, placing it on the September (~Sept 1) agenda. The P&Z Board had recommended the ban 5-1 in late July (exact date pending minutes; separate event held). Delay signals hesitation, not reversal; ban remains pending with the moratorium through Dec 31, 2026 still active.

event_title: Statesboro Planning Commission Recommends Burkhalter Road Data Center Rezoning 5-1
event_description: The Statesboro Planning Commission voted 5-1 to recommend rezoning ~26.5 acres at 6539 Burkhalter Road from R-4 residential to Office & Business for a proposed two-story, 230,000 sq ft data center campus — the first concrete DC proposal inside Statesboro under its June Ordinance 2026-01. City Council decides Aug 18. Striking same-day split-screen with the county BOC tabling its outright ban: city advancing a project while the county weighs prohibition.
project_name: Burkhalter Road Data Center (230K sq ft / 26.5 ac)
source_name: WTOC / Grice Connect / Statesboro Herald / WSAV

event_title: Packed, High-Security Effingham BOC Meeting on Project Camellia; Threats Revealed, Forum and Moratorium Floated
event_description: A packed BOC meeting under heavy security (metal detector, deputies): Chairman Damon Rahn said no commissioners signed NDAs and the county has 'no agreements' with OpenAI (only a routine zoning verification letter per County Manager Callanan). Rahn confirmed staff have received threats since the July 22 announcement and a security directive was issued — though The Georgia Virtue reports none were reported to law enforcement. Commissioner Beth Helmly proposed a full-day Saturday public forum (tentatively Aug 22 or 29, livestreamed) plus a possible moratorium and ordinance review. Rahn defended the IDA against removal calls; Chamber panel planned ~Aug 26.
outcome: Forum proposed; moratorium floated; no county agreements confirmed
source_name: WTOC / WSAV / Effingham Herald / The Georgia Virtue

event_title: Augusta Schedules Three Community Meetings on Draft DC Ordinance — Two Fall After the Aug 18 Target Vote
event_description: Augusta Planning & Development posted a media advisory (Newsflash #4195) scheduling three neighborhood meetings on the Draft Data Center Ordinance: Warren Road Community Center (Mon Aug 10), Henry Brigham CC (Mon Aug 31), and Robert Howard CC at Diamond Lakes, Hephzibah (Thu Sep 3). Two of the three fall AFTER Mayor Pro-Tem Guilfoyle's stated Aug 18 decision target — a signal the ordinance timeline may slip again. The Aug 3 commissioner site visit to an Atlanta-area data center was scheduled the same day; no post-visit coverage has surfaced (held).
outcome: Meetings scheduled Aug 10 / Aug 31 / Sep 3; timeline slip signaled

event_title: Leesburg City Council Adopts 6-Month Data Center Moratorium
event_description: The Leesburg City Council passed a six-month moratorium on data centers, adopted two days before the Aug 6 planning commission review of the city's draft DC ordinance (date derived from WALB reporting; single-outlet, geography unambiguous). City officials say no data center plans are currently pending. First logged DC event for Lee County in this dataset — note the county BOC's own moratorium-extension status (reported under consideration in May) remains unresolved.

event_title: Leesburg P&Z Recommends Disapproval 4-1 of Draft DC Ordinance as Too Weak
event_description: After roughly an hour of resident pushback that the draft ordinance (special permits for industrial buildings over 50,000 sq ft or 1 MW, developer-funded infrastructure, noise/odor/setback rules) was too weak, the Leesburg Planning Commission voted 4-1 to recommend DISAPPROVAL. City Council final vote set for Sept 1; if an ordinance is approved, the moratorium auto-lifts. Residents Megan Childs Weaver and commissioner John Clay led the stronger-regulation push.

event_title: Maysville Adopts 180-Day Moratorium on Future Data Centers (Retro — Missed by Prior Cycle)
event_description: The Maysville City Council adopted a 180-day moratorium on data centers covering FUTURE projects only — it does not affect the already-approved Northern Data/Rumble 120 MW site. Formalizes the July 6 direction to the city attorney. RETRO ENTRY: adopted ~July 21 (published July 22), inside the prior cycle's window but missed; captured via Main Street News in this cycle's sweep.

event_title: Maysville Council Meeting Collapses in 14 Minutes After State Approves Northern Data Land-Disturbance Permit
event_description: At the Aug 3 council meeting, Bureau Veritas' Hal Chitwood announced the Georgia Soil & Water Conservation Commission approved the Northern Data/Rumble land-disturbance plan (clearing/grading only; pre-construction meeting Aug 4), triggering crowd shouting. Mayor Richard Presley adjourned after 14 minutes with most of the agenda unaddressed; the police chief threatened one arrest. Fourth contentious Maysville meeting in two weeks.
outcome: Land-disturbance permit approved; meeting adjourned amid protest

event_title: 100+ Residents Pack Lake Blackshear Library Over Liberty Data Centers' Americus Plans; Petition Drive Launched
event_description: More than 100 residents overflowed the Lake Blackshear Regional Library over Liberty Data Centers' planned facility in Frank Myers Industrial Park (Swett Avenue; land conveyed to the Sumter County Development Authority). Speakers included James Malphrus (SOWEGA Aquifer Alliance), ex-infrastructure engineer Kevin Dowling, and Kirk Lyman-Barner, who launched a petition (scc4t.com) for a permitting moratorium. Mayor Travis Rush said the council is 'working hard to understand the implications.' Date approximate (Aug 4-5; ATR published Aug 5).
project_name: Liberty Data Centers Americus (Frank Myers Industrial Park)

event_title: Liberty Data Centers Publicly Shares Americus Project Details — 150 Jobs at ~$80K Average
event_description: Liberty Data Centers made its first substantive public disclosure of the Americus project: roughly 150 jobs at an average salary near $80,000. First developer-side engagement after weeks of citizen-driven coverage; the project at Frank Myers Industrial Park now has both an organized opposition (scc4t.com petition) and a public economic case.

event_title: Lowndes Ordinance Draft Due End of August; County Rules Out Moratorium
event_description: County Manager Paige Dukes said the county-specific DC ordinance (noise/light, setbacks, water) being drafted from sample ordinances will be ready for public review by end of August — advancing the July 28 directive with a firm deliverable — and stated no moratorium is contemplated, no project is approved or planned, and no NDAs are signed. Residents remain skeptical. Related transparency progression: LAKE obtained the REZ-2025-11 Coleman Road North rezoning materials via open-records request ($40.85 after a $250 quote) — materials absent from 2025 board packets.
project_name: Lowndes DC ordinance / DC BLOX-Langdale watch
outcome: Draft due end of August; no moratorium; records released

event_title: Marietta Council Approves Powers Ferry 18 MW Data Center 5-2 With Noise and Water Conditions
event_description: After the July 8 tabling, the Marietta City Council voted 5-2 to approve rezoning for the 18 MW data center on the ~11-acre site at Powers Ferry Place — with conditions including sound silencers, independent noise testing, and a ban on using city water/wastewater. Standing-room-only meeting with protests over noise, Rottenwood Creek, and utility costs. The application pre-dated the city's six-month moratorium and was exempt from it. Four independent GA outlets confirmed.
project_name: 1155 Powers Ferry Place Data Center (18 MW)

event_title: Roswell Adopts UDC Data Center Amendment 5-0 on Second Reading
event_description: The Roswell Mayor and Council adopted (5-0, second reading; first reading July 27) the Unified Development Code amendment defining data centers and setting noise, water, and energy-consumption standards — capping the process that began with the January 12 moratorium, two extensions, a 27-page staff white paper, and two public hearings. Sourced from the city's official Roswell Connections recap plus Council for Quality Growth.
source_name: Roswell Connections (City of Roswell) / Council for Quality Growth

event_title: Floyd County Commission Holds First Reading of Data Center Ordinance — Heavy Industrial Only, Closed-Loop Cooling
event_description: The Floyd County Commission held the first reading of its data center ordinance: data centers allowed only in Heavy Industrial zoning, closed-loop cooling prioritized, and water reclamation/reuse required for water-cooled equipment. Second reading, public comment, and final vote set for Aug 25. Delivers on the June 80-day moratorium's promise; three Rome outlets confirmed.
outcome: First reading held; final vote Aug 25

event_title: Augusta Holds First Community Meeting on DC Ordinance at Henry Brigham Center
event_description: Augusta Planning & Development held the first of three community meetings on the city's first-ever data center ordinance at the Henry Brigham Community Center (2463 Golden Camp Rd). Residents pressed on noise, water, power bills, and the pace of the process; the QTS Gordon Highway project was reiterated as exempt from the moratorium. CORRECTION to the merged Aug 3 event's description: Henry Brigham was the Aug 10 venue (not Warren Road — Warren Road is Sept 3; Robert Howard CC at Diamond Lakes is Aug 31).
outcome: First community meeting held; two more scheduled

event_title: Dozens Rally Outside Statesboro City Hall Against Burkhalter Road Data Center Rezoning
event_description: Dozens rallied outside Statesboro City Hall on Saturday against the 4AM Development ~27-acre Burkhalter Road data center following the Aug 4 planning commission 5-1 recommendation. Organizer William McDaniel vowed continued pressure ahead of the Aug 18 City Council vote.

event_title: DABC-Commissioned Study Projects $1.2B Investment From Burkhalter Road DC Ahead of Aug 18 Vote
event_description: A Statesboro Herald deep-dive disclosed the Development Authority of Bulloch County's commissioned Economic Impact Group study: $1.2B 10-year investment, 12 jobs, ~$76M combined 10-year net benefit to city/county/schools. Developers Bobby Bagwell (Augusta) and Charles C. Way (Savannah) have applied to Georgia Power for 99 MW; no end user identified. Date approximate (article assets dated Aug 12; interviews 'this week' before the Aug 18 hearing).
project_name: Burkhalter Road Data Center (4AM Development, 99 MW applied)
outcome: Study disclosed; Aug 18 council hearing posted

event_title: The Current Publishes 'Anatomy of a Secret Coastal Georgia Data Center Deal' Investigation
event_description: The Current published a detailed investigation into how the OpenAI Project Camellia land-and-power deal at Savannah Gateway Industrial Hub was assembled under NDAs without public input — with Georgia Power brokering and Effingham officials negotiating out of public view. GPB republished Aug 12, amplifying statewide. Fuels the transparency backlash ahead of the county's planned forum.

event_title: Effingham Launches 'Water Done Right' PR Campaign; Savannah Riverkeeper Pushes Back
event_description: Effingham County launched a Facebook campaign defending Project Camellia's closed-loop, surface-water-only cooling design. Savannah Riverkeeper countered with three concerns — chemical-laden loop drainage, water demands of new power generation, and stormwater runoff — and OpenAI responded point-by-point. County-vs-watchdog messaging war now running in parallel with the formal review process.
outcome: PR campaign launched; Riverkeeper concerns aired

event_title: GA EPD Holds Virtual Hearing on Plant McIntosh Air Permit for TWO New Gas Units — One More Than PSC Approved
event_description: Georgia EPD held a virtual public hearing on the July draft air permit for two additional combined-cycle units at Georgia Power's Plant McIntosh — one more than the PSC approved in Dec 2025. SELC's Jennifer Whitfield criticized the 'optionality' and the cost/pollution risk, explicitly tied to data center load including Project Camellia. Hearing outcome and comment counts not yet reported (held on this cycle's capture date).
project_name: Plant McIntosh expansion / Project Camellia power
outcome: Hearing held Aug 14; outcome to be reported

event_title: Science for Georgia: 81 Proposed Data Centers Could Demand 29-58 GW — More Than the State Can Supply
event_description: The Current and GPB co-published Science for Georgia's analysis (Amy Sharma): 81 proposed data centers statewide, only 25 with disclosed power needs; projected demand of 29-58 GW versus ~14 GW of newly permitted Georgia Power generation — meaning proposed demand may exceed what the state can supply. Georgia Power responded that OpenAI must curtail when the grid requires. The 81/57/25 tracker figures are the best statewide pipeline tally to date.

event_title: Americus Mayor Defends Liberty DC Deal, Discloses $1 Land Sale, Rejects Moratorium Calls
event_description: Mayor Travis Rush gave the Americus Times-Recorder an on-record interview defending the Liberty Data Centers deal: no city tax abatement; the Payroll Development Authority sold the Frank Myers Industrial Park site to Liberty for $1.00 under a use agreement with generator-run restrictions and job minimums; the city ordinance is drafted but not yet passed. Rush rejected the moratorium petition ('moratoriums are problematic') and denied being offered anything improper after Councilman Dowdell's bribery-law question to the city attorney.
outcome: Mayor defends deal; $1 land sale disclosed; ordinance pending

event_title: NPR/GPB Feature: Cross-Partisan Anti-Data-Center Organizing Unites Albany and Mitchell County
event_description: NPR Morning Edition ran GPB reporter Grant Blankenship's feature on cross-partisan anti-DC organizing in southwest Georgia: Albany's city manager on tape denying any DC deal exists, and organizer Lauren Dorminey rallying majority-Democratic Albany residents to join majority-Republican Mitchell County's opposition to a natural gas power plant tied to the DC boom ('we all drink water, and we're all on the same aquifer'). National amplification of the SW GA aquifer-politics story.
project_name: Albany/Dougherty + Mitchell County gas plant opposition

event_title: Flint Riverkeeper Files Intent to Sue QTS Fayetteville Over Water Pollution
event_description: Flint Riverkeeper threatened legal action against the QTS data center in Fayetteville (Fayette County), filing a notice of intent to sue over alleged water pollution affecting the Flint River watershed. First environmental-litigation threat against an operating/under-construction metro Atlanta data center in the dataset.

event_title: Georgia Power-OpenAI Project Camellia Contract Takes Effect by Operation of PSC Filing Rule
event_description: The Georgia Power-OpenAI electric service contract for Project Camellia (3.2 GW / 25-year, filed July 15 under the PSC's April 2025 large-load rule) reached its August 14 auto-effective date. Under the rule, the contract takes effect 30 days after filing absent commission action, and no PSC intervention had been reported as of capture. ANALYST-APPROVED ENTRY: logged per the auto-effective mechanism described by Commissioner Hubbard (The Current, Aug 4) with no confirming coverage yet of the effective date itself — subject to correction if late PSC action emerges. The Aug 13 NRDC/Sierra Club/SACE objection (STATE-20260813-001) did not stay the effective date.
outcome: Effective by rule ~Aug 14 absent reported PSC action
source_name: The Current GA (mechanism) / PSC filing rule

event_title: NRDC, Sierra Club, and SACE File Formal PSC Objection to Georgia Power-OpenAI Contract
event_description: NRDC, Sierra Club Georgia, and the Southern Alliance for Clean Energy filed a formal objection with the Georgia PSC to the Georgia Power-OpenAI Project Camellia contract, arguing inadequate ratepayer protections against stranded costs and insufficient clean-energy commitments ahead of the contract's Aug 14 auto-effective date. ANALYST-APPROVED ENTRY: sourced from SACE's own release and CleanTechnica (non-GA outlets); GA signals are the PSC venue and Georgia Power counterparty. Exact filing date approximate.
outcome: Objection filed; contract effective date not stayed

event_title: Microsoft Unwinds Tax Abatements at East Point, Palmetto, and Douglasville Data Center Sites
event_description: Bisnow and AJC report Microsoft is unwinding property tax abatements at its metro Atlanta data center sites — East Point and Palmetto (Fulton County) and Douglasville (Douglas County) — forgoing incentive structures amid the mounting political backlash against DC tax breaks (including the Fulton BOC's Aug 5 anti-abatement resolution). ANALYST-APPROVED ENTRY: publication dates ambiguous (Aug 6-9); event date approximate to Aug 8. Douglas County site covered in description; logged under Fulton where two of three sites sit.
project_name: Microsoft East Point / Palmetto / Douglasville abatements

event_title: Six Atlanta Councilmembers Introduce Data Center Task Force Resolution (Retro)
event_description: Six Atlanta City Council members introduced a resolution creating a Data Center Task Force to conduct a 90-day study of data center impacts on the city — infrastructure, water, power, and land use — before further zoning decisions. ANALYST-APPROVED RETRO ENTRY: introduced ~Aug 3 (week of Aug 2; date approximate), inside the prior cycle's window but missed; confirmed via Center for Civic Innovation and the city's legislation portal.
project_name: Atlanta Data Center Task Force resolution

event_title: Commission Chair Candidate Cambry Wood Proposes 180-Day Data Center Moratorium (Retro)
event_description: Columbia County commission-chair candidate Cambry Wood publicly proposed a 180-day data center moratorium, directly challenging the county's Google-anchored development posture three weeks after the Columbia County Data Center end-user announcement. outcome: Proposed by candidate; no commission action

event_title: Fulton BOC Votes 5-0 to Oppose Tax Abatements for Data Centers (Retro)
event_description: The Fulton County Board of Commissioners voted 5-0 (sponsor Bridget Thorne, co-sponsor Bob Ellis) to adopt a resolution opposing tax abatements for data center projects and urging all development authorities in the county to decline such incentives — citing $150M in Development Authority of Fulton County breaks since 2020 (~half to Microsoft) and ~$1.1B statewide sales-tax cost in 2026. Zoning power remains with Fulton's 15 cities. RETRO ENTRY: vote occurred Aug 5 (inside the prior cycle's window but missed); confirmed via the county's own Aug 10 release, Center for Civic Innovation, and CBS Atlanta.
